1.4.2.2.2.2.8 The Problem of Distinguishing Fashioning Power From Random Bases
In alleged physicalist random formation of the limited universe and its fashioning elements, there is a group of things which are formed because of special distribution of things T. There is also a larger group of things which allegedly are distributed by default in a non-special way. The origin of non-special distribution is not to be questioned. Let us question from a different angle, this non-special distribution and its relation to what we observe:
Let us take the example of a jet airplane. What is the criteria to find out whether it has been fashioned? Is its fashionedness undetectable except if traced back to its fashioner? Is it so especially if its fashioner is reducible to random things?
Here, to give a possibility to a random basis and being able to ask the above questions we make two key assumptions. 
(1) There is a layer which randomly produces random structures. 
(2) This layer is separable from that which whose fashionedness is assessed: if only the parts of that layer which are also part of the jet are separable, then the airplane can be considered built on randomness, otherwise the airplane and the randomness layer are one unit and whether they are fashioned must be assessed as a whole. 
If (2) is true, then the jet is not the randomness basis. Yet, this can only be trivially true, and this may be so in an emergentist kind of materialism. Then the jet is only coincidental as in the duck example in the earlier part where the billiard balls which misleadingly look like a duck. Even though the billiard balls look like the duck, the duck is epiphenomenal and only the balls are allegedly effective. The duck is just a view of the billiard balls. If this is true, then we are not fashioning jet airplanes, we just look like fashioning jet airplanes. This does not change no matter whether the balls move in deterministic patterns or indeterministic ways. 
On the other hand, if the balls and the duck are all considered to be distinctly effective under any materialist approach, this means that they interact and that they constitute a whole system. In this case, there needs to be another separable layer upon which the above duck and billiard balls behave as explained above, because as the duck is not reducible to the balls, either the materialism which reduces things to the matter -in our example to the balls- is wrong, or there is another kind of balls to which the earlier balls and the duck are reducible; otherwise, the duck would have distinct and effective power over the matter, the matter which according to the materialism is the only effective. 
So, either (1) one is epiphenomenal the other is effective and fundamental hence there must be a distinct layer among them, or (2) they interact and they form a system to be explained in a probabilistic way therefore there needs to be another layer beyond them. Therefore, for either one of (1) and (2), and any version of any of the two there needs to be another layer, and, this will lead to infinite regress. 
As a result, in any case, a randomness basis -denominator for the calculation of any probabilities- and upon that a complex system -no matter how complex it is-, does not work. 
Also, under the above assumptions, even if we know all about the limited universe, it becomes impossible to distinguish that which has been fashioned from that which has not been. Therefore, the most complex and the most simple are indistinguishable regarding whether they have been fashioned. But if fashioning is not impossible, then at least some things may be fashioned, and if they are fashioned then they are effects or they contain effects of fashioning. 
So, if our assumptions entail not perceiving/ measuring the effects of fashioning, then our assumptions must be false. Or fashioning must be impossible. But fashioning is not only possible, but also we fashion things continually.
1.4.2.2.2.2.9 Full Randomness is Unfalsifiable and Unverifiable, Partial Randomness Entails the Existence of Transcendent Cause
If our free will power or reasoning or consciousness are true and/or distinctly effective, then the randomness basis can have at best only limited and partial effect on the organized layer. Because when a free will power owner fashions something, or if his consciousness or reasoning has any distinct effect in the limited universe, this is at least partially a result of neither randomness nor deterministic patterns.  
So, is partial randomness possible? Even if it might allegedly be possible, it would not be a principle. Then at least partial transcendent cause is possible, but if a partial transcendent cause is possible, then the alleged random things also may be caused by the transcendent cause, since, the random events need such a cause as explained in part 1.6.2.1.1.2. 
If partial randomness is impossible, that is if everything must be based on randomness, then this latter is an unfalsifiable claim, it has neither empirical nor logical basis, since we know the entire limited universe neither in all its spatial extensions, nor in its temporal extensions, nor in its structural extensions.
What is the threshold of complexity of a thing above which we should say that that thing has been fashioned? If we actually observe a maximum thinkable complex structure within what the human beings fashioned or in nature and outside of what the human beings fashioned, should not we conclude that that structure has been fashioned? According to the arguments of the materialists, no matter what the degree of the complexity and the specific organization of any structure, we should not conclude that it has been fashioned. Because there �may� be a kind of a multiverse or a kind of an unknown which may make the random formation of that structure reasonably probable; or even if there is no such reasonable probability, it is possible that a tiny probability may have happened. So, for the materialist, no degree of complexity and organization may be a reason to believe that that thing has been fashioned. The materialist may consider this as a strawman, yet, according to the tools and methods the materialists use to explain fine tuning, we can allegedly explain any kind of complexity by probabilities.
On the other hand, if a materialist says that above a degree of complexity we should conclude that that thing has been fashioned, then we would ask �why would not a complexity above that threshold be produced by a randomness, while something below it would be?�
So, no matter how high the degree of organized or specified complexity, randomness as its cause is not detectable. Hence, an explanation of any complexity based on randomness is not falsifiable. 
1.4.2.2.2.2.10 A Random Event is Necessarily Caused. 
Some claim that according to the quantum physics� findings, things may happen without any cause at all. Yet, they say that a certain atom decays at an unpredictable time. Hence, they are not talking about something that comes into existence out of nowhere, but a change in the spatiotemporal position of �something�. Think of your chair moving without any cause at all to the right; is it correct to say that there is no cause for it? 
Suppose that a falling rock sways allegedly randomly to the right and to the left while it is falling. Suppose that there is no magnetic forces or other patterns causing it. So, can this swaying be explained within the limited boundaries of the rock? Does the rock cause it self-sufficiently?
No, because these are changes with respect to other things. The changes have specific values though they are allegedly random. The changes entail the behavior of many parts in a specific direction in spacetime, and relatively to other things. Hence, saying that it happened without cause is similar to saying that a falling rock falls without a cause. Hence, the explanations in part 1.1.2.2.2 about the laws of nature are applicable in this respect.
The elements of the changes are within a whole which is unified. In accordance with the explanations about the property of Unity in part 1.2, the behavior of the rock is caused.
1.4.2.2.2.2.11 We Should be Consistent in our Decision Methods Related to Likelihoods.
When we buy a car there is a likelihood that the seller is a fraudster and has cooperated with the government or notary officer to wrong the buyer. But we do not stop from buying that car because of that likelihood. The likelihood of many things and fashioning aspects happening by themselves is much less than the probability of fraud in this example. So how should we behave with respect to the fashioning elements? Should not we behave as we do in our daily lives? Why should we divert from our daily method?
If when we buy a car we do not investigate each related party thinking that the probability of all of the related parties collaborating for a fraud against us is negligible and act accordingly, then should we consider that the formation of the limited universe has a non-negligible probability?
1.4.2.2.3 Brute Fact
Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.
(Quran: 41/42)
Some say that the fashioning elements and their possible causes are just brute facts, and they suspend judgment. Adopting the idea of brute facts is abandoning truth. Because then a person ceases questioning things, and looking at things from different angles. Yet to reach truth we have to look at things from different angles and they have to pass the tests from all angles and must not fail by inconsistencies or contradictions. Because truth is consistent from all angles. 
For example, if we see 30 marble balls distributed on the table so as to write �I love you� we say �there is an intelligent being involved in this�. But the physicalist evolutionist comes and says: �Wait a minute. There are billions of balls, so on the contrary it is  likely that there is such a statement without the involvement of an intelligent agent.� The theist says: �But there is nothing around, which brings the parts of the balls to produce the balls other than the intelligent beings�. An atheist says: �Well, the balls are brute facts, you are not allowed to question them.� This is an example, but overall, it is what happens against God�s fashioning.
If one adopts the fashioning elements and their causes as brute facts, without assessing their relation to other facts, then he will have adopted some facts and considered them as superior over others emotionally or without reasoning. However, it is possible that the opposite facts are true and not questioning some of them will qualify such a person as someone who does not follow the truth.

On the other hand, the alleged runners of such simulations would be running those simulations with the sustaining power and permission of the One Fashioner.
Hence, this suggestion does not work either as an explanation which tries to explain the fashioning elements we observe by the contents of the material world.

1.4.2.2.7 Multiverse
The multiverse is a key objection against the higher degree of fashioning of the limited universe, though it is not any such objection against the fundamental fashioning. 
The motivation for a multiverse is as follows: If the universe is just one of the many universes, then the seemingly small likelihood of the occurrence of these complex relationships will not be so small. After all, if I roll the dice once, it may not be very likely to get 6&6; but if I roll them 50 times, then the likelihood of the result of one of the rolls being 6&6 is much higher compared to the previous scenario. According to the anthropic principle, human beings would naturally be in a successful universe.
The flaws of the multiverse as an objection against the Fashioner property and other properties of Allah are explained in part 1.1.2.2.2.14 about multiverse.
1.4.2.2.8 Evolution
Above, I explained that our observations about forms, relations, wholes, contingencies entail a fashioning power. Some of the important observations related to fashioning relate to the living world. So, a key counterargument against the claim of the fashioning by God, against the claim that the source of fashioning is not ultimately within the limited universe, is evolution. 
Based on evolution, some people claim that the fashioning considered as an explanation for the living world is no more than something which only looks like fashioning, and that in fact there is no real and effective fashioning underlying the life forms. In parallel with this, even what we fashion also becomes the result of an evolution which supervenes upon and originates from the physical events. Furthermore, there are even claims that the universe as we see it, is a product of some evolution.
So, one of the key arguments against the fashioning and creation by Allah is the evolution. While an atom or a planetary system can also be used as evidence for their being created by a transcendent being who encompasses the future and many elements in His unity, harmonizes them, and balances them, the extreme examples of wisdom in creation are seen in life forms. Moreover as we are one of the life forms and observe that we did not create ourselves, although we can design many things, makes the claim that the life forms are designed, created, and sustained by a Wise Creator more compelling. When an eye, the brain, a neuron, an enzyme, a DNA, a motor protein, or any other system in life forms are proposed as an evidence for their being created, the counter argument is that the evolution is sufficient for their existence, hence there is no need for a Fashioner to design and create them, therefore they are not evidence for God. Furthermore, the possibility of evolution being true is also used in order to refute the claim that the numerous systems in life forms are evidence for God.
And often those who try to debunk evolution try to do it based on the considerations about the complexity of life units and the unlikelihood of their formation randomly. However, although the extremely complex life forms and life related processes make this approach useful, it is not essentially conclusive. Because, mostly the related data is either missing, or hidden within billions or hundreds of millions of years ago, or is within yet undiscovered or undiscoverable details of infinitesimal biological systems. The physicalist evolutionist may always claim that the transitional fossils are yet to be discovered or have been destroyed; or that the components of initial cells may have come from somewhere in space where there are complete graduality and all elements of physicalist evolution. Or they may claim that the segments of the DNAs endogenous retroviruses in the same locations of DNAs of chimpanzees and human beings demonstrate that they have common ancestor while it is yet to be discovered that the 3D dimensions of human DNA or molecular structures and processes or selective processes do not permit the random integration of those segments in different locations of DNAs.
And the proponents of physicalist evolution have a room to argue that this unlikelihood of the self-sufficient rise of life is because of our lack of knowledge, and that the more we learn, the more likely will the rise of life forms through chemical processes be. If it is only unlikely, we often see some things which were once unlikely and which became likely in the future. Unlikelihood depends on our knowledge. For example, 500 years ago if one was told that a person will speak to another person hundreds of miles away while seeing him, this would be considered very unlikely. However, when we learn about the physical entities and relations, we see that far from being unlikely, that communication is directly experienced by almost every human being. So, it is important to see whether there are any empirical, logical and principle-based contradictions, gaps, and problems in physicalist evolution which make it impossible, independently from what will be discovered in the future; and this study shows that there are.
But are we condemned to ambiguities that prevent us from reaching final conclusions about the debates on evolution? As we will see in the following, the answer is no. There are many clear ways that may lead us to ultimate conclusions on this topic.
In this context, this section will attempt to show that there are contradictions not only within the terminology and logic of physicalist evolution, but also between them and the empirical facts. And it will establish the errors related to the use of evolution against the existence and certain acts of God. This section is a refutation of an evolution which is defined and interpreted as an argument against God; it is a refutation of an evolution which is given as an answer to a question of a believer �who created the human being�. It is not a refutation of a God-neutral study of fossils, relations between species, mutations... 
So, let us examine evolution in detail in this context. 
1.4.2.2.8.1 Relevance of Evolution to the Fashioning Power of Allah.
He (Allah) created the human being.
(Quran: 55/3)
A key question that leads many people to God is �who created me, since I did not create myself?� Some answer this question by saying �God�. 
And some believe that the correct answer to this question is not God, and that it is �the random mutations and natural selection, namely evolution�. This answer is given not only about the human beings, but also about all species. There are even theories which try to explain our limited universe in terms of a Darwinian evolution of the cosmos116. For the physicalist, a physicalist interpretation of evolution is incompatible with God, because the life is explained by the matter: Whether the matter and the laws of nature need God is a separate issue, hence if these are put aside, for a physicalist (or materialist), matter and laws of nature are sufficient to produce life, hence, regarding life, God is redundant. 
This answer is closely related to the approach of explaining all living things within the limited universe in accordance with physicalism. Note that here physicalism means reductive physicalism that reduces life including its allegedly emergent properties to the physical or spatiotemporal relata and relations; and as explained in part 1.1.2.2.10 of this book, non-reductive physicalism is not fundamentally different than reductive physicalism. If this approach is successful and correct, then at least regarding the life forms, God does not have any effect, hence in this respect, there is no evidence for God, and God would not be the Fashioner of the life forms. Evolution may also be presented by some as an alternative to God even though it is not presented as a disproof of God; in other words, it is claimed that the life forms �may have� appeared through evolution as well, hence, they have no evidential value for the existence of God.
When evolution is discussed in the debates about God, it is considered as a black and white issue. The materialist tries to prove that it is true although he inconsistently considers it in many respects as a holistic fact; the theist tries to disprove it as if his religion necessarily entails its rejection entirely, even though an alleged evolution has many holistic aspects which would make it a sub-proof for God and His fashioning power.
Indeed, in the Quran we see that the human beings came from a single couple, while in the same book we also see that the differentiations of the colors of human beings are presented as evidence for Allah:
Among His evidence are the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the variations in your languages and your colors. In these, there are signs for the knowledgeable.
(Quran: 30/22)
So, if there are systematic variations in the color of human beings while all human beings originate from one man and one woman, and if those variations are guided by Allah, then why should we say that God would not create certain things through these variations, and that He would stop these variations when there is a transition to something �we� call a new species? Consequently, some consider evolution as a process driven by God, see it as compatible with belief in a Creator and Sustainer God. Is this consideration reasonable? If the differences in our colors are evidence of Allah, does not this entail that mutations is one of the methods Allah uses in creating living beings and some of their new traits?
Is God unnatural or supernatural, is He disconnected with the creation? The word �natural� in natural selection, and �random� in random mutation are mostly understood as statements opposing God. Materialists generally try to emphasize a distinction between natural and supernatural and then to refute the supernatural. Evolution is presented as something natural as opposed to a supernatural God. I am personally against considering God as an unnatural or a supernatural Being, since if He is true, He is the only Creator and Sustainer of the nature, and strongly related to the nature. 
At first sight, the adjective �natural� may seem unproblematic against belief in God. But in fact, it is a redundant adjective if it is not considered as something used against God, to denote a substitute for God for representing Him as �unnatural� or �supernatural�. -However, note that there may also be god claims like a �human god� who is both mortal and immortal; in such cases god may be considered as unnatural or supernatural since there is an obvious discrepancy between what is natural and there is no way to reconcile that natural with that type of god.- Clearly, naturalists and atheists interpret and represent the adjective �natural� in this second way with respect to �natural selection�, as something against the Fashioner property of God, and against the fashioning sub-argument. 
On the other hand, the word �random� in random mutation is obviously incompatible with a God who has power over all things and a God without whose permission nothing may happen; so, saying that some �random� things and events may or do happen without the sustaining, permission and control of Allah, is against the Islamic teaching. Therefore,  the evolution according to this materialistic understanding and representation, is incompatible with God and monotheism.
So, the above show that the construction, definition, and classification of the concept of evolution is not mature and clear enough. I explain in detail in part 1.4.2.2.8.4.2 that a distinction between �physicalist evolution� and �God-fashioned evolution� is necessary; and that such a distinction would make the related debates more productive, precise, focused, and would make evolution more understandable and analyzable. If one goal of science is to find the causal relationships, an assertion that the involvement or the likelihood of involvement of God within the rise of species cannot be examined by science �s is far from being scientific; it is only the result of a non-scientific world view.
The materialist uses the word evolution as a �reductive� evolution, and reduces the life forms to the molecules and particles, which is incompatible with belief in Allah. It is unlikely that a disbeliever adopts a God-fashioned evolution, since, this kind of evolution would be recognizing that there are transcendent and holistic source(s) of the rise of life forms.
Although the materialist adopts a physicalist and reductionist evolution when arguing against God, he in any case needs to use holistic facts to explain this evolution. He necessarily explains �wholes� at a certain layer by reduction to �wholes� in another layer, he uses �relations�.
The theist may adopt a holistic evolution at least partially without contradicting the belief in a God Who creates and sustains all life forms. The physicalist may also claim to be using a holistic evolution, however, as the following parts explain, at the end of the day she will have to reduce the holistic elements to their physical parts.
Evolution is not the opposite of Islamic creationism. Allah may create through evolution as well. But a physicalist evolution defined as reducible to allegedly self-sufficient spatiotemporal bottom elements is against Islamic creationism.
A God-fashioned evolution understood as a partial process which is controlled, directed, and sustained by Allah may be acceptable or even necessary to some extent according to Islam. God-fashioned evolutionary processes may influence some or all species under the guidance of Allah and/or under the freedom permitted by Allah to His creation at different layers in some respects and along with some patterns. 
There may be a theist who believes that God is active only in the realm of laws of nature and macro things like the creation of the universe, hence that God�s creating life forms may be done by Him indirectly. However, according to Islam, this kind of evolution is not acceptable. Because according to the Quran, Allah is active in the creation of each species and creature. 
Can this Divine activeness be reduced to the initial state of the universe? Do the life forms arise through a deterministic unfolding of the God-determined initial or quasi initial state of the universe? This is inacceptable in Islam, since, Prophets prayed and people are encouraged to pray to get good progeny. One may say �maybe Allah does this by knowing the future and adjusting things at the initial state of the universe�; however, this is not very compatible with the teaching of the Quran, since there is no reason for claiming that the power of Allah should be limited to the initial stage. 
Hence, evolution as natural selection through random mutation essentially contradicts Allah, His properties and acts as taught in the Quran in many respects like sustaining the patterns, autonomies of life forms, their consciousness, and so on. Here, �random� is used to correspond to chance or unguidedness, and this point will be further clarified below. In this respect, natural selection may be a means by which the creation is directed to some extent in some ways and in interaction with the distinct effectiveness of transcendence and free will power of the life forms. But randomness in mutation is not acceptable as the following parts will explain in detail. In any case, mutations are directed and/or sustained though there may be free will based mechanisms and entities sustained by Allah at many layers and although these mechanisms may relate to behaving in accordance with the laws of nature established by Allah.
Accordingly, in the considerations and discussions about God, if evolution comes up as an argument, first the parties must specify whether they mean by evolution the physicalist evolution or the God-fashioned evolution. So, instead of an overall ambiguous definition of evolution, some work needs to be done about distinct definitions of �physicalist evolution� and �God-fashioned evolution�. This point about this distinction will be explained in detail in the following parts.
Question 61. 
If Allah fashions human beings in the wombs however He wills, then what about the drugs or operations which influence the growth of the human beings in the wombs?
Answer 61. 
Obviously drugs, x-rays and many other factors influence the growth of a human being in the womb. However, none of  these are outside the control of Allah. If some parts of the physicalist evolution are true, then whatever the human beings do are the result of the initial state which has been fashioned by Allah. If physicalist evolution is false, then the human beings and other factors may be influential about how the human beings are shaped in the wombs of their mothers. But in this latter case again, all of the factors would be sustained by Allah, and He would be active at any layers.
With some technology, we can make robots which reproduce, and feed themselves. Will they have evolved? Obviously not. So, if God made the beings and ran evolution like a mechanic process, is it not by definition no evolution? So, by definition, cannot evolution be a matter of fashioning? In other words, if an intelligent being organized the processes by which things improve or undergo natural selection, then would not this be evolution by definition? If it would not be evolution, then what can be the justification that an evolution must have nothing at its origin any fashioning? Because without such a justification, evolution would be excluding arbitrarily in its definition any process which is influenced by the involvement of intelligent beings. Then, this would be just an emotional approach far from being rational. In this case, we cannot say that evolution is God-indifferent; such an evolution would be a physicalist evolution and developed as a tool against God.
But if the robots we made evolve according to their design, are considered as the products of evolution, since we are allegedly products of evolution and reducible to the material, then evolution is not something that necessarily replaces fashioning, if we are truly fashioning things. Because, in that case, the robots would be both the result of our fashioning, and evolution which happens according to our design. So in this interpretation, if we are truly fashioning things, then physicalist evolution cannot be brought in as an argument against the divine fashioning. In other words, if we are products of evolution and if we fashion things, then a process of evolution we fashion would be a product of both evolution and intelligent fashioning.
However, if the improvements or adapted changes of those robots which improve are considered as no evolution because of our intervention through our fashioning, then we cannot say that physicalist evolution is true unless we demonstrate that no God is involved in the structures of atoms, molecules� 
Also note that life is not the only or extreme example of transcendent unity and fashioning of Allah, it is only one of the good examples. So if physicalist evolution was successful, it would be in any case partial and incomplete as an argument against the Fashioner. 
Question 62. 
What are the implications of the explanations in this part with respect to Adam and Eve peace be upon them (PBUT)?
Answer 62. 
The issue of whether Adam and Eve were created as the Quran says is automatically solved when we have solved the general issue of physicalist evolution. Because when we understand the distinct effectiveness of life forms at life layer and their being created and sustained by Allah, then it will be very easy to recognize the normality of Allah's creating Adam and Eve (PBUT), since He is the Creator of all life forms.
When this book talks about evolution, it does not talk merely about Adam and Eve (PBUT). Their distinct creation does not affect the truth or falsity of evolution: If a scientist would produce a new life form in the lab, it would not affect the evolution. Likewise, if evolution is true as a God-fashioned evolution, then it will not be any argument against the creation of Adam and Eve (PBUT) as detailed in the Quran, since there is no necessity that every being is created through evolution.
Jesus Christ (PBUH) made a bird out of clay, and breathed into it and it became alive; obviously, as a living bird, it would have DNA and other features of the kind of the bird it was. Even today, humanity tries to produce life out of mere matter. 
Though we do not know the exact details of Adam and Eve (PBUT), the details that we know about them are compatible with our current scientific knowledge: For example, one scenario is that Allah created Adam like He created a bird in the hands of Jesus Christ (PBUH); and then He may have created Eve (PBUH) using Adam�s genetic material. 
In this context, one may ask �there are human-like fossils that date back to hundreds of thousands of years or even millions of years according to some, so how does this fit with the creation of human beings from one man and one woman�. The distinctive mental capacities of human beings unmatched within the living world demonstrates the special origin of human beings. Concerning the timing and relationships with other human-like beings there is no enough evidence. They may be really humans and the one man and one woman may be at the origin of those �human-beings�; or those beings may have gone extinct before that one man and one woman; or they may have gone extinct in their struggle against the generations from Adam and Eve (PBUT); or another scenario that we missed may have happened.
There is no 6000 year constraint in Islam as the life of the earth or of the universe. And there have been 224000 prophets to mankind according to one hadith. The following verse clearly explains the Islamic teaching in this respect:
O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
(Quran: 49/13)
Topics that relate to human beings and evolution, such as endogenous retroviruses, shared body plans between human beings and other organisms, and vestigial organs in humans have been explored by other authors and experts. While these specific discussions will not be addressed directly in this book, the arguments presented herein will indirectly address these subjects as well.
So there is no problem in their literal existence and creation.
1.4.2.2.8.2 Scenarios of the Origination of Species
How can species on earth originate? If we consider all theoretical possibilities even the unlikely ones, we can have a better understanding about what alternatives entail which conclusions, and which ones are irrelevant or practically useless.
If there is no principle that necessitates that the only ways for the rise of species are the random mutations and slight variations they produce, then we can understand that instead of randomness, bigger and holistic systems may be at work. 
So, let us imagine the theoretically possible ways prima facie in which new species may arise:
1. Creating out of Nothing: 
In this scenario, the creation of life would be like a male and a female rabbit popping out on a rock out of nowhere. 
This scenario represents a theoretical possibility under materialism. Lawrence Krauss strongly defends the hypothesis that the universe may have come from nothing. Although his nothing is not really nothing but a kind of quantum fluctuations, he claims that the universe with all its contingent properties has come out of nothing. If the atoms, electrons, or other particles can come out of nothing, then obviously some kinds of life forms also may pop into existence out of nothing as well. 
In Islam there is no ontological general nothing since Allah is Eternal. So, life forms cannot come out of nothingness. But there are or there may be things other than what we perceive, which occupy no place in our knowledge and perception; if what we do not have access to is called a kind of epistemological nothing, then Allah may create life forms from that realm:
And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except according to a known measure.
(Quran: 15/21)
So, there does not seem to be any fundamental problem with Allah�s creating life forms out of such nothing. However, we see that even the first human beings who have been created in an exceptional manner were not created like that, but they were created from already existing material. If every species that faced difficult conditions were individually replaced in an ad hoc manner and popped out into existence, this approach would represent a less unified mode of creation. 
2. Origination Directly From Matter, Like Clay:
This scenario possible according to the Quran as we read in the following verse:
And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay.
(Quran: 23/12)
Actually, the evidence available today suggests that matter is a composite of fields interacting in specific ways. Hence, while inanimate matter may be considered a less functional and less complex set of fields, a living being that embodies that matter may have totally different properties on top of the inanimate matter. Therefore, the creation in this context could be akin to the infusion of certain properties into that living being that transcend beyond the matter embodied in it thereby imbuing it with a distinct identity like the unique characteristics given to an individual electron. The following verse is relevant in this context:
He (Moses) said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it.
(Quran: 20/50)
As opposed to each species first members popping into existence out of �nothing�, and then going extinct upon changes in conditions, and then other species popping into existence anew, a system in which species can adapt to changing conditions appears more efficient and coherent. Nevertheless, there is no principle against the theoretical possibility that traits and organs arise in accordance with a certain plan through a certain communication and interaction between certain realms:
He made ears, eyes and hearts for you, but you give Him very little thanks.
(Quran: 32/9)
Yet, obviously, our organs are created through certain processses within the wombs of our mothers; however, as indicated above, it is obvious that numerous properties and acts are effective in the creation processes of those organs on top of the properties and acts of the inanimate matter. Likewise, in the creation of each being numerous epigenetic processes like DNA methylation, genetic modifications also happen. Those are far from being chaotic as can be clearly observed through sophisticated techonologies we have today. The following parts will explain in detail the reasons for the irreducibility of those processes to the behaviors of the inanimate matter.
Scientifically also creation based on the matter is a probable origin of life forms directly from some matter (non-life). This is called abiogenesis. Since at a certain stage, our planet did not contain life as generally known, this is the broadly accepted special way of the origination of life forms on earth. But the question is whether the inanimate matter is self-sufficient for the origination of life, or whether the inanimate matter itself as well is created and sustained by a Transcendent Being and whether this Being also works on the life forms as He works on the inanimate matter.
3. Creating From Existing Life Forms:
When a new being is to be created, should God always create from the inanimate matter? Or would He create using an infrustructure like genetic material and create other beings through such mechanisms? We see in the Quran that the latter is within the power of Allah:
He created you (all) from a single person: then created, of like nature, his mate; and he sent down for you eight head of cattle in pairs: He makes you, in the wombs of your mothers, in stages, one after another, in three veils of darkness. Such is Allah, your Lord and Cherisher: to Him belongs (all) dominion. There is no god but He: then how are ye turned away (from your true Centre)?
(Quran: 39/6)
The work of the God on the inanimate matter or on the life forms does not need to be fully ad hoc. Especially to facilitate understandability and utility of the things in every creature�s environment, it is possible that all creation is sustained within a global system wherein there are also some patterns like metabolism, reproduction, repair mechanisms. 
If Allah had created new species from matter for each different condition, then this would be probably not as wholistic, beautiful, and effective as creating a system wherein beings may adapt to changing conditions. For example, if a species of bird went extinct because of change in the environment color, and Allah could not change it so that it might continue its existence when some changes arose in the environment, and He needed to create a new species of bird which would survive under the new color setting, this situation would be less wholistic compared to a situation where that species survived by changing its color in the newer offspring. But in any case, Allah would be sustaining the process which would produce the new system. But the more wholistic case would be more resilient and understandable by the creation especially by the human beings. Otherwise, there would be continual surprises for all kinds of creation, and there would be a less intelligible and more ad hoc involvement-requiring situation for Allah. There would be less unity, control, and connection. Imagine that a member of a new species like an elephant popped out into existence out of nothing in your bedroom, or that your armchair tuned into such an animal: such a world would have lots of shortcomings. But having a system where there are genetic mechanisms and slacks that allow code-based mutations that may with the design and command of the Creator cause also bigger changes in body plans and other traits in a way that would allow the first members of new species benefit from their ancestors habits and supports seem to be more plausible, functional, cooperative, and effective. It should be noted that a similar mechanism built on random mutations and complete graduality is not supported by the evidence as briefly explained in part 1.4.2.2.8.5.1.17.2.
The situation where there is some adaptation capacity of the life forms though this capacity is sustained by Allah seems to be more unitary, divine, and beautiful; it also has more evidential value for a common creator of all life forms. The following verse is more related to a comprehensive unitary system:
The creation of you all and the resurrection of you all are only as (the creation and resurrection of) a single person. Verily, Allah is Hearing, Seeing.
(Quran: 31/28)
It should also be noted that there is no reason to say that God cannot or will not create or may have created any new life forms in ways other than the above.
We see that the Quran not only recognizes the changes in the human form, but also presents them as signs which show His powers:
Among His signs are the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the variations in your languages and your colors. In these, there are signs for the knowledgeable.
(Quran: 30/22)

The above might also be happening abruptly and in ad-hoc ways, but we generally do not observe such changes. Creating such different human beings in a systematic and integrated way demonstrates a higher creating power since it requires bigger harmonization of numerous constraints: for example, we can produce numerous car parts separately; but to make them such that they can work together harmoniously as a car requires bigger capacity.
This method exemplified in the changes of some properties of some human beings is also recognized by the modern science.
Creation from already existing life forms may happen in two ways:
a. Creation of New Species Through Reproduction
The above may happen gradually or abruptly. If pregnant women have been subject to radiation as in the case of Chernobyl disaster, their babies may incur big changes in their DNAs which may result in physiological and other changes. These changes would be normally harmful changes. If similar changes occur with other babies and if two such babies marry when they grow up and if they are fertile, then it is possible that there is a group of people with big variations.
Can different circumstances cause that a baby male tortoise is born from a couple of cats? Maybe not under normal conditions where DNA repair and control mechanisms work well. But it might be possible though very unlikely, under exceptional conditions, since every newborn undergoes numerous mutations. But there needs to be a female and a male tortoise for the continuity of the species of tortoise. Is this possible in the above extraordinary situation? Even a male baby tortoise being birthed from a cat is highly unlikely, and we do not observe such things happen. Yet, through hundreds of millions of years, theoretically such things may have happened even though it is not very likely.
Anyway, the existence of fertile hybrids like clymene dolphins, wolphins, and beefalos demonstrate that new species may have been created outside the allegedly gradual evolutionary processes. Again, the relatively recent discipline of epigenetics also show that within a single generation drastic changes may happen, even though the changes related to gene expression is evolution is still a matter of debate: on one hand these changes are related to gene expression, on the other, the related mechanisms should have a place in the genome.
b. Creating From an Existing Life Form Through Methods Other Than Reproduction
Creation from an actually existing grown up life form as happened with the formation of Eve peace be upon her (PBUH). However, this is presented in the Quran as a special case, and probably it is not a systematic way to create new species.
Cloning methods used today can be a contemporary example of such creation.
4. Changing Already Existing Life Forms. 
Existing living beings may be transformed into other beings as indicated in the Quran:
And you had already known about those who transgressed among you concerning the sabbath, and We said to them, "Be apes, despised."
(Quran: 2/65)
Theoretically, this can also happen through technology.
5. Transfer of Life From Other Planets/ Galaxies (e.g., Panspermia).
This is irrelevant in our context, because, even if it happened, the life in the planet from where the life we observe was transferred or the civilization that produced life would be subject to the same questions about the origin of new life forms that we try to answer.
We cannot say that 1, 2, and 3 are impossible; and we cannot say that if they happen they are not driven by God unless we are all-knower about all infinitesimal details. 
The above alternatives may happen theoretically in one of two ways:
1. Randomly: This requires that consciousness and other transcendent properties of life forms are reducible to the matter which is defined by its distribution and separation in space and time. Because of the incompatibility of this separation with the unity and transcendence we observe in at least some life forms and because of the reasons explained in part 1.6.2.1.1.2 a random rise of life forms is not plausible. One may ask, how can the technological change cited above can happen randomly: The answer is that if all things in the universe are reducible to the matter and its purposeless spatiotemporal relations, then the technological involvement of human beings or other beings will also be random.
2. In a guided/ sustained way: This is plausible and possible, although some will argue that the guide/ sustainer would also need a guide/ sustainer in an infinite regress. However, if we have the designing/ fashioning capacity on top of the allegedly random movements of the matter, this means that we already have a different category. So, the creation by transcendent powers would be happening in any case. The question whether this power arises from nothingness or through infinite regress is a question of a different category which is explained in the relevant parts of this book.
Consequently, we can say that at the beginning some life forms may have been created in special ways. However, afterwards, it is possible that a holistic and sustained evolutionary process may have happened at least partially.
1.4.2.2.8.3 Types of Evolution Relevant in the Context of This Book
There are many types of evolution such as macro evolution, micro evolution, quantum evolution� 
However, in the context of this book, I will focus on two types of evolution: the God-fashioned evolution and the physicalist evolution. God-fashioned evolution, if wholly or partially true, is the evolution whose elements such as the life forms, properties, entities, processes are sustained by Allah, and that are not fully reducible to the spatiotemporal, in other words to that which is defined by the spatiotemporal relationships. Physicalist evolution is the evolution whose corresponding elements at the layer of life are allegedly reducible to the spatiotemporal.
The following analysis will show that physicalist evolution is false.
The following analysis will also show that if God-fashioned evolution is true, it is not only compatible with the properties and existence of Allah, but also it is a component of the proof of Allah and His fashioning property. However, I will not give a big emphasis on whether God-fashioned evolution is true or not, since, no matter whether it is true or not it is not an argument against the fashioning power of Allah, and if it is true, its aspects that prove Allah are already contained in all things.
Physicalist evolution is based on a hidden and contradictory dichotomy: 
(1) If that which allegedly evolves is reducible to a reduction basis, then:
-It does not evolve since it is just a shape of the things at the reduction basis layer, 
-Something effective at the reduction basis does neither evolve nor change, 
-Evolution is just a view of the state of the things at the allegedly effective reduction basis. 
If something totally ineffective, epiphenomenal, and reducible to the things in other layers and especially in the reduction basis layer is studied by evolutionary biology, then it will not lead us to the truth, since, any time, it may be discovered that the working of another layer entails totally different results. 
If the reduction basis evolves, in other words if the physicalist evolution is true concerning the reduction basis, then either that reduction basis is reducible to another reduction basis, or it does not evolve in accordance with the physicalist evolution. So, if there is no infinite regress regarding physicalist evolution, then physicalist evolution is false. But if there is infinite regress, it is again false since a causal infinite regress is impossible as explained in the part about infinite regress. 
(2) If it is not reducible to a reduction basis although there are lower layers, then there is at least some top-down causal influence, hence, the effect of the top is not sustained entirely by the reduction basis, but in some respect directly by a different and transcendent sustainer. 
The evolutionary theory that is criticized in this book, is a derivative of and in parallel with reductive physicalism. However, note that non-reductive physicalism is also essentially reductive as explained in part 1.1.2.2.10.
1.4.2.2.8.4 Definition of (Biological) Evolution
1.4.2.2.8.4.1 Popular Definitions of Evolution 
Some popular definitions of evolution are as follows:
1. Descent with modification from preexisting species: cumulative inherited change in a population of organisms through time leading to the appearance of new forms : the process by which new species or populations of living things develop from preexisting forms through successive generations.117
2. Change in the gene pool of a population from generation to generation by such processes as mutation, natural selection, and genetic drift.118
3. Evolution is the process by which the physical characteristics of types of creatures change over time, new types of creatures develop, and others disappear.119
4. [Biological evolution] is change in the properties of groups of organisms over the course of generations� it embraces everything from slight changes in the proportions of different forms of a gene within a population to the alterations that led from the earliest organism to dinosaurs, bees, oaks, and humans. (2005: 2)120 
Note that the above popular definitions diverge fundamentally about their core, about what is that which changes. 
Likewise, there are big debates in literature about what is the unit of selection as we see in the following quote:
He (Richard Dawkins) remarks, in fact, that the debate about group versus organismic selection is �a factual dispute about the level at which selection is most effective in nature,� whereas his own point is �about what we ought to mean when we talk about a unit of selection� (1982a: 46).121 �effective replicator will be a very large chunk of DNA� (Dawkins 1982b: 89; Sapienza 2010).122
The two concepts at the core of evolution theory are the natural selection and random mutation. However there are also concepts as �extended evolution� which comprises also the epigenetics.
The above give us some initial hints about the evolution as something situated between physical and biological layers. 
So, let us see now some important points regarding the definition of evolution:
1.4.2.2.8.4.2 A Distinction Between God-Fashioned Evolution and Physicalist Evolution is Necessary
When a believer and disbeliever in God debate about evolution, one saying that he believes in it and the other that he does not, what do they really mean by evolution? If the disbeliever means by it a totally purposeless process reducible to the behaviors of atoms, then the believer in God if he is consistent, cannot even accept the microevolution that is accepted by most believers in God. But if it is defined as an irreducible process where the agents who are allegedly the outcome of that process are not reducible to the behaviors of particles, then the disbeliever in God cannot believe in such an evolution while being internally consistent since such an evolution would necessitate the recognition of a Sustainer Who would sustain different irreducible beings with irreducible, distinctly effective powers, and irreducible properties. Therefore it is necessary to emphasize the need for distinction in this respect: when one debates or thinks or conceives evolution, what kind of evolution concept is it? A physicalist evolution according to which life and its beings, processes are reducible to parts and particles that may or may not cause emergent properties at higher layers? Or an evolution where life and related beings, processes, and properties are not reducible to the parts, hence need to be sustained by a Transcendent Sustainer Who sustains those beings, processes, and properties at all layers? 
Note that here the physicalist evolution corresponds to a reductionist evolution, and God-fashioned evolution corresponds to a non-reductionist or holistic evolution. Throughout this book, physicalist evolution will be used corresponding to reductionist evolution in this context, and God-fashioned evolution will be used corresponding to a holistic type of evolution and vice versa. A physicalist evolutionist may also claim that he is not reductionist though he is a physicalist evolutionist; however, a physicalist evolution is fundamentally reductionist as explained in part 1.4.2.2.8.5.1.4.2.
One of the key points with respect to the distinction between physicalist evolution and God-fashioned evolution is randomness. Although random mutation is at the heart of the current evolution theory and neo-Darwinism, and the word �random� in �random mutation� means essentially purposelessness or unguidedness, it is likely to see that there are people who claim that evolution is neutral regarding a Creator or Sustainer of it. On the other hand, many aspects of evolution may be true while it is sustained, designed, and guided by a Creator, Designer and Sustainer God. The distinctions are sometimes made under the terms of �guided evolution �  unguided evolution� or �theistic evolution � non-theistic (or secular) evolution�.
The key word in this respect is �random�, since the other key word �natural selection� is not any source for the rise of traits which will lead to new species. Natural selection is only functional in the elimination of inefficient traits or life forms. 
In this respect, Gregory (2009) explains the word �random� in �random mutation� as follows: �In particular, mutations are known to be random (or less confusingly, �undirected�) with respect to any effects that they may have. Any given mutation is merely a chance error in the genetic system, and as such, its likelihood of occurrence is not influenced by whether it will turn out to be detrimental, beneficial, or (most commonly) neutral.�123 
If this description of the word �random� is true with respect to the essence of evolution, then obviously a general usage of the word �evolution� becomes God-incompatible: In other words, random mutations are sufficient sources of evolution and sufficient relevant elements of its definition, hence there is no need for God for the rise of the new species. 
However, it is not exceptional to meet people who claim that evolution is God-neutral. For such people, if the theory of evolution is true, this does not entail that a God directs it or not; evolution theory deals only with what is observed, and it does not say anything about what happens behind. Such people may also be using an idea of a deistic God who started the universe then sat back, or a God Who just sustains or designs the laws of nature without having any intention for life forms. Regarding Allah this approach is not acceptable since Allah is the Creator of all life forms. On the other hand, there are also people who claim the same God-neutrality of evolution although they have in mind Allah as the God. Obviously, a random and unguided mutation which is considered sufficient to produce new traits hence new species is incompatible with a life-creating God.
So, if a believer in God also believes in the control of evolution hence random mutations by God, he should be considering that the �randomness� in those mutations is not a true unguidedness, but rather an unpredictability of the results of the mutations. Such randomness or uncertainty is a popular interpretation in physics where a non-trivial group of physicists recognize that the uncertainty in quantum physics is no more than our unability to predict because of our limitations in our measurements and related tools.
Could we consider evolution as if it were unrelated to 'randomness'? Given that randomness is a core element of evolution, we cannot. Suppose I were to move each subatomic particle of a group of bacteria in a way that imparts new traits for future generations, would those bacteria have evolved? They would not, since the key processes and properties of evolution would be missing.
Consequently, since neither the theistic nor the non-theistic evolutionist would want to contradict his definition of evolution with his conclusions, we can say that there needs to be more than one definition of evolution.
One may claim that the theistic type of evolution is not scientific; in other words, we cannot use �evolution� as in the sentence �the cars evolved�, where the cars are passive and human beings design their evolution. Because if evolution is like this, then we could not use natural selection as an effective mechanism, since the cars are totally passive with respect to their makers. Because the struggle to survive and the resulting natural selection is effective if evolution  theory is true. But again contradictorily, if natural selection and random mutations are true causes of evolution, then these contradict the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution which claims to explain the complex by the simple, which claims to explain the things at the life layer by things at the lower layers. 
However, as long as there is no evidence for the undirectedness of the mutations, this claim is not necessarily true and it is also built on unevidenced personal preferences. The materialist may say that the one who makes a claim must present proof or evidence. However, the claim that the mutations are random is also a claim to be defined, proven, and evidenced if it is claimed to be true.
Moreover, this is not the only divergence in the understanding of evolution between the theistic evolutionist and non-theistic evolutionist: The theistic evolutionist may make use of transcendence-related properties such as consciousness, knowledge, free will, purpose and so on while the non-theistic evolutionist will need to reduce the evolution to the lower layers. After all, for the non-theist there is no source to get these transcendent properties other than the matter defined by spatiotemporal relations.
Although the above key differences exist among experts on evolution, when people talk about �evolution�, they generally think that everybody means the same thing with �evolution�. However, this is not the case. The definitions of evolution differ, what is understood from evolution in its elements differ, and what is understood from it in different contexts differ. Evolution deals with life, which is one of the most difficult and controversial issues. And it tries to answer questions through studies that covers hundreds of millions of years, through the layers of biology, chemistry, physics, through science, philosophy, science, theology, reductionism, and holism. Hence, we can anticipate that it will not have an easy definition that is acceptable to all.
If it is difficult to have such an aggreed upon definition of evolution, the best way is to have precise definitions so that at least the strengths and weaknesses of each definition and its related assumptions and conclusions may be well understood, and appropriately used in the relevant contexts. 
When life is presented as a creation hence as an evidence of God, evolution is represented by the materialist as an �alternative� which replaces God. Obviously, such materialists consider evolution as something that happens without God. If they accepted that the definition and essence of evolution is God-indifferent, then they would not be arguing in this way, and the relevant relata, relations, properties of life would be left unquestioned and unexplained. So, they must be adopting a definition of evolution that entails the non-involvement of God; furthermore, they claim that this way they are adopting a scientific approach while in fact it is a subjective opinion. 
If evolution is defined such that there is no factual component of evolution that entails that God does not get involved with its running and design, it is totally plausible that a believer in God, agrees with some aspects of evolution and disagrees with some of its other aspects like the professionals of evolution agree and disagree on some of its aspects.
Therefore, especially when evolution is used in the context of God, it is necessary that each party clarifies what he or she means exactly by evolution, by presenting the distinctive elements and features of his definition. Moreover, if evolution should be defined to give a complete picture related to its truth, its definition must inform us in broader contexts also about whether it happens with God or not. One might argue as �should we add the component of God or no God in the definitions related to science such as the definition of gravity and so on?� Obviously, in the contexts of applied sciences that component may be overlooked since whether God established the related patterns or whether they are self-sufficient will have no implication for instance when we are building an airplane. No matter whether one believes that gravity is an unquestionable brute fact as a permanent law of physics, or that it is something that may be hopefully valid for the next year, or that it is an element of the divine design, he or she can be an engineer in that area. But if we use gravity in a debate about God, then whether it is self-sufficient or not will be directly related to that debate: if it is conceived by the debaters as something happening self-sufficiently will be completely relevant to the debate. 
Note that here the �definition� means a comprehensive �real definition� and an understanding about what it is, not a simple dictionary definition. �Real definition� is clarified by Gupta 2021 as �Fine 1994 defends the conception that a real definition defines an object by specifying what the object is; in other words, a real definition spells out the essence of the object defined. Rosen 2015 offers an explanation of real definition in terms of grounding: the definition provides the ground of the essence of the object.�124 Gupta 2021 also quotes the following from John Locke to clarify what the real essence is: �the real essence of gold is �the constitution of the insensible parts of that Body, on which those Qualities [mentioned in the nominal essence] and all other Properties of Gold depend.� 125
The following will explain that the physicalist adopts a reductive (reductionist) definition of evolution as opposed to a holistic definition of evolution entailed by the God-fashioned evolution. Because if the transcendent properties of life such as consciousness are not grounded in and caused by the material/ spatiotemporal, then at least another ground with such properties will be necessary; such a ground obviously does not comply with the physicalist approach which asserts that God has nothing to do with evolution. So, when evolution is used as an argument against the existence and involvement of God, then this is a physicalist evolution. When used in this way, it is used to mean implicitly or explicitly that evolution explains or may explain life and properties observed within life only based on atoms, molecules and ultimately by the most fundamental forms of matter and without any fashioning and sustaining of Allah. 
There are also agnostics who claim that though it is not clear that God has not fashioned the living things and their properties, there is no convincing reason that God has fashioned, created, and sustains them. The evolution adopted by agnostics who �behave� as if there is no God and use this line of reasoning as a basis for these conclusions, should be considered as physicalist evolution as well. Because for them, there is no impossibility that the truth is as entailed by physicalist evolution.
On the other hand, a believer in Allah who ascribes some possibility to evolution will need to adopt a holistic definition of evolution since for him, Allah is active in creation without the need to act only through any deterministic and physicalistic channels.
Some definitions of evolution are God-indifferent: for example, the definition as �Descent with modification from preexisting species� does not entail that the evolution is reducible to the physical. The 4th definition is similar to it in this respect. 
However, some definitions are reductive: For instance, the definition as �Change in the gene pool of a population from generation to generation by such processes as mutation, natural selection, and genetic drift.� reduces evolution to �change in the gene pool�. Here it is also assumed that �mutation� is random as mostly qualified. 
On the other hand, the definitions have a mixture of holistic and reductive elements: For instance, the words as �organism�, �species� represent wholes and not aggregates, even though aggregates also have holistic aspects. But words like genes and processes represent some reductive aspects, though genes and processes also have holistic aspects though in different layers. Hence, I argue that no definition of evolution can escape being holistic. However, we must recognize the fact that in the same time the physicalist adopts contradictorily a reductive definition which reduces the life to other things.
One may argue as: �Evolution is a scientific theory, it does not claim anything against or for God, as gravity or other laws of nature have nothing to do with God.� Though this may be understandable regarding the usage of evolution in the books of biology, when evolution is put forth as an argument against God, the situation is different. Then its usage is like the usage of laws of nature as substitutes for God, by which many materialists claim that those laws narrow down the range of activity of God. Indeed, when the theist puts forth some biological systems as an argument for God, the atheist brings in the evolution as his main counter-argument. Therefore, the evolution used in this way cannot be considered God-indifferent. Hence, it is important to emphasize that in such contexts, atheists are not employing a God-indifferent evolution, but rather a physicalist evolution. 
Using the term �physicalist evolution� will give the atheist an alleged opportunity to demonstrate that evolution happens without the involvement of God. Because presenting some findings about an alleged tree of life which are god-indifferent and irrelevant to the discussion about God as if they disprove God does not add any value to the discussion about the existence and involvement of God.
On the other hand, distinguishing the claim of a physicalist evolution from a claim of a God-fashioned evolution will also enable the theist to question the additional premises entailed by the �reductionist� aspect of the physicalist evolution126. When the theist brings in the systems within the life forms as evidence of God, he is adopting a holistic approach no matter whether he believes in a God-fashioned evolution or not. If a God-fashioned evolution is true, this evolution would be no argument against his claims for God; only a physicalist evolution could be put forth as a candidate argument against the believer in God. Hence, he may ask the atheist �even if evolution would be true, why does it have to be a reductionist and pysicalist evolution?�
Obviously, whether and when the scholars of evolution will come to a consensus about a definition of evolution that joins reduction and holism is an unknown as of now. It is also possible that it never happens, since they are contradictory. But as it is obvious in many analyses regarding God, those who adopt atheism and agnosticism will mostly use a mostly implicit or explicit reductionist and physicalist definition of evolution, and they will reduce consciousness, free will power, and other transcendent aspects of living things to the spatiotemporal. But those who see God and His transcendence as active in the creation, fashioning, and sustaining of life may be closer to a holistic definition of evolution, though they do not need to accept it.
The debates about evolution with respect to God continue within the ambiguity about what evolution means in this context, what is meant by that which evolves, and what is meant by the effect of evolution. 
When we say evolution, what do we really mean by it? What do we mean by that which evolves? If we are the product of evolution, then what are �we� effectively? Are we passive aggregates of effective particles, or effective sub-particles? Or are we distinct and effective wholes? Are we just the illusory and epiphenomenal perceptions of the really effective particles? If so, when we say evolution do we mean an illusory evolution, while in fact the effective particles never evolve? If we evolve as distinctly effective wholes, and if we are not reducible to or supervenient upon the particles, then from where do our irreducible properties come?
Are the properties of life forms distinctly effective? Or are these life forms reducible to the spatiotemporal entities and events? For example, is consciousness effective? Are the many related qualia effective? Are the tendency and struggle to survive distinctly effective? Are reasoning-like abilities effective? Is knowledge effective?
If the one who argues against Allah using evolution postulates that these are distinctly effective, then, he must be arguing that they are not reducible to the spatiotemporal; in other words, they must not be reducible to atoms, protons, electrons� Because otherwise the particles would be effective instead of the struggle, knowledge, and so on.
Then he will be asked where these properties come from and at what stage they are connected to the relevant life form and individual organism? And how do such transcendent irreducible powers operate on spatiotemporal/ physical laws of nature? If they are reducible to atoms and waves of all kinds of wavelengths, then seeing, hearing, running of life forms that the physicalist evolutionist claims to explain through the propagation of light, sound waves become trivial since the waves themselves would then have properties as consciousness, knowledge, and so on � note that as explained in part 1.4.2.2.8.5.1.4.2 emergentist arguments do not solve this problem �. Therefore, such an evolutionist would not have explained anything new. Furthermore, the laws of physics and chemistry which are assumed to explain life, will in fact be explaining only the physics and chemistry, since the fundamental particles must already have the properties of the life forms. 
On top of that, such a physicalist evolutionist will have to explain the combination of consciousness of a human being�s parts with the consciousness of that human being. 
On the other hand, he will have to accept that as there is the spacetime wherein spatiotemporal events occur, there will have to be a space of consciousness wherein the consciousnesses of things are sustained and operate. Additionally, he will have to explain the origin of that space of consciousness which is necessarily based on unity.
The incorporation of the distinct effectiveness of the facts such as consciousness and free will power will render evolution an evidence for Allah as explained in the relevant parts of this book. Hence, this is not a path that the disbeliever in Allah may take.
There are lots of further related questions that we will see in this part.
The above questions force us to make clear choices in order to define evolution. And these choices compel us also to decide which kind of evolution we accept: An evolution where all the wholes and their properties in the layer of life are no more than epiphenomenal things with no distinct existence and effectiveness? Or an evolution where such wholes and their properties have distinct existence, effectiveness, and interaction with the other wholes in different layers? Hence, a distinction based on reduction and irreducibility becomes crucial.
Therefore, when one says that he merely believes in evolution, he is not saying something meaningful and consequential in the context of God; and he is being ambiguous. What kind of evolution does he believe in? Does he believe that he is epiphenomenal and nothing more than his particles/ parts, in other words does he believe in a reductionist, physicalist evolution? Or does he believe that he has a distinct effective reality, and that his effectiveness is as real as that of his particles; in other words, does he believe in a holistic, God-fashioned evolution? 
If he believes in both reductionist and holistic kinds of evolution, then obviously he is saying something contradictory. Because, as we will see in detail in the following, a holistic evolution entails a Creator and Sustainer. But a physicalist evolution entails in parallel with reductive physicalism that everything is reducible to the spatiotemporal/ material; hence, that a Creator and Sustainer is not necessary. 
The contradiction is not limited to the issue of the Creator: if he suspends judgment on what is that which evolves and about the nature of the process of evolution, then his claim is lacking the essentials about the �whatness� and �howness� of evolution. Consequently, anybody who says that he believes in evolution must clarify what kind of evolution he believes in.
What about the one who rejects evolution? A person may be rejecting evolution entirely including the God-fashioned evolution, and believe that God created all species in an instant. When arguing against an evolutionist and assessing evolution, such a person also needs to know what he is arguing against, and therefore, he has to know what the reductionist/ physicalist evolution and holistic/ God-fashioned evolution mean.
At first sight, there are two main theoretical alternatives about evolution: 1. It has not happened. 2. It happened.  Each one of these two alternatives can be divided in two: 1.a. Each species was created abruptly by God 1.b. Each species arose randomly without God. 2.a. Evolution happened by God. 2.b. It happened without God. There is no reason to claim that 2.b is the only way. There is some evidence that some life forms are related and may have evolved at least through microevolution. There is no need according to religious sources that all was created separately and abruptly. There is evidence that there are at least micro changes in species. Note that the denial of evolution does not leave us with a single alternative of creation by God; even if it is denied, again all may have arisen randomly. After all, if a species may arise randomly gradually, it can also happen randomly abruptly at certain moments within billions or hundreds of millions of years. Hence, the key distinction is not whether a species arose gradually or not, but rather whether a species arose randomly, or through the creation of a transcendent Being. Hence, the holistic aspect as opposed to the reductive aspect of creation is a more relevant distinction.
Because of the questions and reasons briefly mentioned above, there needs to be a distinction between a physicalist and God-fashioned evolution.
Question 63. 
If we need to make a distinction based on reducibility and irreducibility/ holism regarding the evolution, then should we also make such a distinction within physics, or within chemistry, or within any of the social sciences? Because for example it is also possible that one claims that economics is reducible to the spatiotemporal, and another one claims that economics has its distinct effectiveness and dynamics. If not, what is the difference of evolution in this respect?
Answer 63. 
These sciences do not have a core aspect of explaining something in terms of a different science. For example, if a scholar of political science concludes in his study that a leftist party generally develops politics against the worker class, he does not say that he explains this based on the elementary particles. He does not say that he explains something social with something physical. Though on some occasions he may use some physical factors; such factors will be ad hoc and not systematic in our context. The issue may be discussed in the philosophy of political science. Or if the physicist explains some behaviors of atoms through the behavior of electrons, he does not claim to explain something physical in terms of another (non-physical) science.  Or if a chemist explains a chemical event with a physical event, he assumes that what he calls �chemical� is in fact a name given to the physical events from a different perspective.
But the �random� mutations, DNA �molecules� are at the core of and indispensable for the evolution. The evolutionist attempts to explain the layer of life and its properties as consciousness, knowledge, survival, species� based on the layer of chemistry and ultimately physics. This is as if an economist tries to explain the stock price fluctuations systematically by the behaviors and properties of protons and electrons instead of supply demand price relations, preferences and so on economical concepts and relations.
So, the study of evolution is fundamentally different than other sciences and requires such a distinction.
