Therefore, if physicalist evolution theory assumes that it does not study just epiphenomenal entities, beings, and events, it will need to recognize the reality of new wholes and their distinctness. Hence, this constitutes another contradiction inherent in physicalist evolution. 
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.4.1 Life-Related Key Properties Whose Ontological Realities and Distinct Effectiveness are Abolished by Physicalist Evolution
Let us see certain irreducible powers and elements that are deprived from their distinct effectiveness by the physicalist evolution.
1. Free Will Power
If for example, a human being has the free will power to choose between canilla ice cream and chocolate ice cream, this means that he does not need to behave in accordance with the behaviors of his particles. If this is the case, then the future generations or species arising from human beings, and from other beings that have free will power do not depend solely on the behavior of the molecules and atoms. Moreover, the free will power cannot have come from the behavior of atoms and other particles. Hence, a distinctly effective free will power and the physicalist evolution are not compatible, and if the free will power can be proven, physicalist evolution must be false. And if we recognize the truth of the physicalist evolution we cannot recognize free will power and its distinct effectiveness. 
The free will power experiments where upper layers are effective on lower layers as explained in part 1.6.2.1.1.3, disproves a physicalist evolution. If at a physical layer (Lp) there is a deterministic trajectory corresponding to a simple law-like trajectory, a free will power owner may will something which entails a shift into different trajectories of particles negating the physically predicted trajectories. Even if we put aside free will power, if the physicalist evolution brings in distinct explanations on top of the physical, then it will be impossible that a trajectory of a living thing and a thing at Lp to always overlap. At some points, the trajectory predicted according to Lp patterns and the trajectory predicted according to the dispositions of the biological layer (Lb) will need to diverge. But as two contradictory events cannot happen at the same time on two layers, then the evolution related processes would override the physical processes or vice versa. If Lp trajectory diverges in favor of Lb trajectory, this means that Lb dispositions are irreducible to Lp patterns; if this never happens, this means that Lb is ineffective hence there is no effective evolution, that there is neither holistic nor physicalist evolution, and all things allegedly explained by evolution are no more than approximations; and the true explanations are at the layer of physics; and that for instance, fitness or survival of an organism or natural selection are just approximate shortcut words with no true explanatory power; and the true and precise explanatory things are at the layer of atoms and sub-atomic particles. As explained in part 1.1.2.2.1, the atoms and sub-atomic particles also suffer from the same problems under reductive physicalism.
Under physicalist evolution, morality and reasoning power are allegedly epiphenomenal and approximate as well. If Lp depends at least partially on Lb regarding the distinct properties of the life forms, this means that life forms are effective hence Lp patterns are not exclusively fundamental hence Lb is not reducible to Lp. If they overlap and Lp behaves both according to Lp and Lb,  this entails that Lp entities behave at multiple layers and interact with things at multiple layers, hence inherently they are both multi-dimensional having also effective dimensions related to logic, morals, consciousness, transcendence, and purpose. The latter point applies if Lb depends to some extent on Lp.
Let us suppose that there is a whole at Lb (WLb) and a whole at Lp (WLp). Let us suppose that there are some instances where the trajectory of WLb depends on the trajectory of WLp; and some instances where the trajectory of the WLp depends on the trajectory of WLb. In this situation, both wholes are sovereign with some degrees of freedom. An example of this situation is an addict who sometimes quits smoking, and is sometimes overcome by the addiction related dispositions of his brain. Under God-fashioned evolution, such situations may arise. Under physicalist evolution, WLb is always slave of WLp. 
If ASBEs follow their trajectories without influencing and being influenced by life forms, then life forms will not be evolving, because light sensitive cells , survival..., adaptation to environment will be non influential, ineffective approximations. ASBEs cannot make life forms do what life forms do. There are at least certain properties of higher layers which are not possible by the properties of the ASBEs; if they were possible, then they would already be inherent within the ASBEs. So, life forms and at least some of their properties like free will, consciousness are not possible by the movements of ASBEs. 
As free will power experiments indicated in part 1.6.2.1.1.3.1.1.2 demonstrate, the life forms are distinctly effective. The lines of waves form in the sea but these are not different than the alleged properties of ASBEs which allegedly move according to certain trajectories. So, saying that other complex orders and patterns may arise from ASBEs is a faulty generalisation. If life forms are reducible to trajectories of particles, then they are not life forms, they do not have design power, freedom, consciousness... We cannot talk of survival of a life form unless it is autonomous and it has free will power except as the survival of a horse shape in the clouds; but obviously we cannot talk of the survival of that shape since it cannot be defined and since what makes it happen keeps its existence and activity even if that shape goes away. Free will power is very important in showing the divergence and distinct effectiveness of a life form from constituents. And free will power requires transcendence, consciousness, knowledge and its existence demonstrates the distinct existence of those properties to a certain extent. Free will power can be had distinctly by higher layer things.
Free will shows that the parts are not fully predictable in and of themselves and reducible, hence also that the whole has distinct existence. Therefore physicalist evolution is false. Part 1.6 shows that free will power exists as a distinct power.
The rejection of free will power by physicalist evolution corresponds to its rejection of the distinct effectiveness of random mutations, eating's... influence on survival. If the distinct effectiveness of free will power is rejected, then the distinct effects of mutation, eating struggle for survival must also be rejected. But the physicalist evolution does not reject all of those, but only some of them; hence it is contradictory.
Free will power is often contrasted to determinism, for example, a main approach called compatibilism considers whether free will is compatible with determinism. However, even if the universe was not deterministic and even if a true uncertainty would be the case at the level of particles, we would not be talking about the free will of the life forms as long as we maintained that our wills are reducible to the behaviors and trajectories of particles. 4. Identity
If you buy a house for yourself, what is yourself? Yourself who will stay it 10 years later will be your today�s self? If Jack committed a crime today and got caught 5 years later, is Jack of 5 years later who will put in prison the Jack of today?135 Are you today �you� of 20 years ago?136
Physicalist evolution that attempts to explain the origin of species destroys even the identity of an individual living being.

The Ship of Theseus is a famous philosophical thought experiment in this context. It questions the nature of identity over time. It is a hypothetical scenario where a ship, undergoes gradual replacement of its individual parts due to wear and tear. As all components of the ship are replaced over time, the question arises: Is it still the same ship? This paradox illustrates the issues around the boundaries of identity and what defines an object's existence in the face of constant change. The paradox arises from a physicalist approach where the purposes, perceptions, identities of the builders and repairers of the ship with respect to the construction of the ship and the replacements of its parts are rejected as distinctly effective things and separated from the ship which is considered only as an aggregate of particles. The purpose of the first ship and its parts are rejected and disconnected. But if we recognize that the first ship was unitarily related to a specific purpose related to certain people, each part related to certain purpose then we could easily classify all things and understand the relations between the initial ship and the renewed ship perfectly.
Furthermore, as underlined earlier, by demolishing the identity of a being within a species, the physicalist evolution also precludes the recognition and utilization of the ontological building blocks of any species and related explanations. Hence, using these as explanations while rejecting them constitutes an important contradiction within the physicalist evolution. For example, if we say natural selection of life forms, here life forms mean not only the aggregate of particles but also the behaviors of life forms like loving, deciding, playing, saving, spending, hearing, enjoying, hunting, escaping, producing, speaking, surviving, struggling... So, if we deny the distinct reality of the human being, then we will ascribe all those acts to the things at the reduction basis layer; such an approach is absurd and contradicts all of our daily empirical observations.
Many powers and properties some of which have been given above cannot exist on their own. They belong to an essence or substance. The effects related to a property must be affected by that object or being. The things at the reduction basis layer cannot have those unitary properties. 
5. Reason
Physicalist evolution undermines rationality. If we claim to be rational and to be the outcome of physicalist evolution, then the evolution must be having processes more than the random ones. But obviously, the physicalist evolution cannot have processes more than the random ones; after all, the core of physicalist evolution consists of random/purposeless mutations.
Hence physicalist evolution is self-defeating: If we claim that it is true as a limited scientific theory, and if we are the outcome of random processes, then our claim that it is true collapses, since our claim would be only epiphenomenal, and would not be free from the irrational movements of the underlying particles. Arguing for physicalist evolution entails that the words of the physicalist evolutionist are not random, nor the result of chance nor of deterministic processes, but contradictorily he also claims that they are reducible to such processes. In other words if he claims to be reasonable, he and his origin and his foundation at the ultimate layer would not be random nor deterministic. If they were random or deterministic, then he could not claim to be in harmony with the truth. If physicalist evolution rejects reason, then it will reject any claim for or about physicalist evolution as well.137
The above point is just an example. To put it more generally, we should consider the fact that if our decisions supervene upon the behaviors of blind particles, then there is no basis to claim that our conclusions are reliable. Indeed there are often disagreements on many points, and each party claims to be closer to truth. However, if we are reducible to the trajectories of particles, then we cannot claim that any point of view is closer to truth. One may say that we are producing computers that give us accurate results; however this is not a counterargument because the computers are produced by human beings and this argument is built in the rejection of physicalist evolution: the correctness of the laptops is obtainable because human beings who make them are not reducible to the trajectories of particles.

Tectonics, like chemistry, does not have autonomous laws of its own like life forms. Tectonics, like chemistry, does not have freedom or free will of its own. But if I make a choice about what to buy at what price, the rules of my choosing what to buy are different than the rules of my atoms. A particular decision about it may be considered as irrational even though my atoms will behave always according to their proper laws or probabilities. Those atoms move in any case as they allegedly have to move according to their properties and laws, but I may be behaving as I ought not to behave. I may have made an irrational decision, but since my atoms will overlap with it for example in its conception or in its effects than we cannot say that I was economically irrational. But obviously I may be truly irrational. So if I evolved to behave in accordance with the survival of the fittest through natural selection I will have behaved either rationally or not at the layer of human beings. I must have evolved at some point. But if physicalist evolution is true there cannot be better structure. Because particles behave as they need to. 
A perfect circle will be defined by ASBEs and nothing more ultimately if physicalist evolution is true. Then it is the distribution af ASBEs in spacetime. If the latter, then can there be incorrect or correct economics decisions? If the ASBEs behave as they must do according to laws of nature, then there is no possibility of behaving in accordance with rationality or reason, since I would not have free will to override the ASBEs. 6. Knowledge
Physicalist evolution poses a challenge to the concept of transcendental knowledge. It undermines the notion that we can possess knowledge about the world beyond ourselves. If we subscribe to the idea that our existence is a result of reductive processes governed solely by randomness, then our claims to knowledge become questionable. After all, how can we trust the reliability of our conclusions if they are merely epiphenomenal and subject to the irrational movements of underlying particles?
Consider the field of astronomy. Through careful observation and scientific inquiry, astronomers have amassed a vast amount of knowledge about the universe. They have studied celestial bodies, discovered distant galaxies, and unraveled the mysteries of black holes. Yet, if we adhere to physicalist evolution, we must question the validity of this knowledge. How can our understanding of the cosmos be trusted if it is reduced to the random movements of particles within our brains?
The pursuit of scientific knowledge itself becomes questionable under the lens of physicalist evolution. Scientific progress relies on the accumulation of knowledge through experimentation, observation, and theory-building. We rely on the assumption that our scientific endeavors are uncovering truths about the natural world. However, if our reasoning and knowledge are reducible to the behavior of particles, then the reliability of scientific knowledge collapses. Our discoveries would be mere outcomes of random processes, lacking any basis for claiming their truthfulness.
Furthermore, the development of complex systems and technologies challenges the reductionist perspective. Take the example of computer programming. Through the systematic arrangement of code and algorithms, programmers create software that performs intricate tasks. The functioning of these programs relies on knowledge and understanding that surpasses the deterministic behavior of individual bits and bytes. The programmer's ability to design and optimize algorithms demonstrates a level of knowledge that transcends the reductionist view of physicalist evolution.
In the realm of art and literature, we encounter works that convey profound insights about the human condition and the world we inhabit. These creations offer unique perspectives, emotional depth, and cultural significance. Appreciating and interpreting these artistic expressions requires a level of knowledge that cannot be reduced to the random movements of particles. Our ability to engage with and derive meaning from art and literature points to a transcendent understanding that extends beyond the reductionist framework of physicalist evolution.
In conclusion, physicalist evolution undermines our capacity for transcendental knowledge. It calls into question the reliability of our understanding of the world and challenges the validity of scientific discoveries, artistic expressions, and the accumulation of knowledge across various domains. The richness of human knowledge and our ability to comprehend and engage with the world around us point to the existence of a transcendent unity that cannot be reduced to the random movements of particles.
One may argue against the randomness above based on natural selection and claiming that natural selection which is a key process in physicalist evolution, is not random, hence arguing that physicalist evolution is not random. However, while it is true that natural selection plays a significant role in shaping the course of evolution, it is important to recognize that the underlying mutations that fuel the process are indeed random. Natural selection acts as a filter, favoring beneficial mutations that increase an organism's fitness and survival while eliminating those that are detrimental. However, the occurrence of these beneficial mutations is fundamentally random and unpredictable.
Random mutations form the raw material upon which natural selection acts. They arise from errors in DNA replication, environmental factors, or other stochastic processes. While natural selection guides the direction of evolutionary change by selecting advantageous mutations, it does not determine or generate these mutations themselves. The randomness of mutation is inherent in the very nature of molecular processes and the probabilistic outcomes of genetic variations.
The key point here is that while natural selection brings a non-random aspect to evolution by favoring certain traits over others, it operates on the foundation of random mutation. The selection process does not eliminate the randomness of the mutations themselves but rather acts as a sorting mechanism, preserving beneficial variations and discarding harmful ones. The combination of random mutations and selective pressures gives rise to the complex patterns of biodiversity we observe today.
Therefore, the argument that natural selection negates the randomness of physicalist evolution is misleading. While natural selection may introduce order and directionality, it cannot escape the fundamental randomness that underlies the generation of genetic diversity. The role of natural selection is to refine and fine-tune the outcomes of random mutations, but it does not eliminate the stochastic nature of the mutations themselves.
Additionally, natural selection is ultimately an epiphenomenon resulting from the behaviors of lower-level particles, waves, quarks, or fields governed by the laws of physics. It suggests that the effectiveness of natural selection is not an independent and causally effective force but rather a product of underlying physical processes. This perspective challenges the notion that natural selection possesses inherent agency or causal power in shaping evolutionary outcomes.
At its core, natural selection relies on the differential survival and reproduction of individuals with advantageous traits, leading to the accumulation of beneficial traits in populations over time. However, the driving forces behind this process lie within the fundamental interactions and behaviors of particles and fields at lower levels. These particles and fields adhere to the deterministic laws of physics, which govern their movements and interactions without regard for the specific outcomes of natural selection.
In this context, natural selection can be seen as a passive consequence or side effect of the behaviors and properties of the particles and fields. While it may appear effective at the level of organisms and populations, it ultimately supervenes upon the lower-level processes and lacks independent causal efficacy.
Furthermore, the argument against emergent properties reinforces the epiphenomenal nature of natural selection. Emergent properties are often viewed skeptically, as they are seen to lack causal powers or explanatory capabilities. If natural selection is considered an emergent property, it would inherit these limitations, suggesting that its perceived effectiveness is illusory and ultimately derived from the behaviors of lower-level constituents.
By acknowledging the epiphenomenal aspect of natural selection, we recognize that its outcomes are determined by factors beyond its control. The behaviors and interactions of particles and fields at lower levels dictate the possibilities and constraints within which natural selection operates. Consequently, the notion of natural selection as a driving force of evolution becomes secondary to the underlying physical processes.
In conclusion, the argument for the epiphenomenal aspect of natural selection highlights that its effectiveness is derived from the behaviors of lower-level particles, waves, quarks, or fields governed by the laws of physics. Natural selection, while appearing influential at the level of organisms and populations, can be seen as a passive consequence of these underlying processes. Hence, natural selection cannot be used to justify any consistency of any knowledge claim that �may allegedly be� the result of physicalist evolution. 
On the other hand, sometimes, some creationists present certain information like that in the DNA as a challenge against physicalist evolution or abiogenesis. However, the issue lies not with the specific information itself, but with the concept of information as an irreducible entity. If information is merely reduced to the medium in which it is encoded, then the question of its origin becomes irrelevant, as there would be no true information, only particles colliding with one another.
Further details about the knowledge and its irreducibility are given in part 1.8.
7. Properties Specifically Related to Morals
Physicalist evolution abolishes properties related to morals. Some of those properties obviously relate to the properties already examined above like free will power and identity. However, there are also properties that are specific to morals which are not examined above, like altruism, truthfulness, keeping one�s promise, fairness, responsibility, compassion, respect, and honesty and their opposites.
If the human beings and other living beings and species are solely the result of the trajectories, movements, and interactions of particles, and if the latter are the only effective, then the properties related specifically to morals become just names given to certain types of trajectories of those particles and waves. Those properties become just epiphenomenal, and since our epistemology also is according to physicalist evolution reducible to those trajectories and behaviors, then the properties specifically related to morals have no implications at all.
However, in our daily life we observe that those properties make a difference in many contexts. Therefore, physicalist evolution contradicts our daily experiences. If a person has a conflict between his altruism and egoism then you can think that his altruism has resulted from the random processes of evolution but that it gives a competitive advantage to his community. But as at the origin the altruism resulted from the random behaviors of evolution then it may be rational for him to choose the egoistic behavior because he may not expect to see the positive consequences of his altruistic behavior personally. But according to Islamic understanding his feeling good for doing an altruistic behavior or any other behavior correlates with a unitary harmonious fundamental truth.
Moreover, there is also an internal contradiction of physicalist evolution in this respect since if physicalist evolution is true, then those properties must have arisen because of some distinct effectiveness. If we claim that honesty �ought to be� promoted, or �injustice� ought to be prevented, then obviously these relate to the survival of a being or of a society. If we argue that promoting honesty or preventing injustice is necessary for the survival and well-being of individuals and society, then attributing these moral imperatives to the behaviors of particles presents an inherent inconsistency within the framework of physicalist evolution. Hence, reducing those properties to the behaviors of particles or waves constitutes also an important inconsistency within physicalist evolution.
This part will not repeat the properties that are also closely related to morals like free will: for example, without free will we cannot talk about the responsibility which is a key property directly related to morals. Again, the property of �ought to be� is also an important issue related to morals that is related closely to the purposefulness of living beings and that is examined under the property of purposefulness.
Moreover, physicalist evolution also undermines key higher properties related to morals such as �objectivity�, �subjectivity� and �relativity�: not only objective morals is to be left according to physicalist evolution, but also the subjective morals as well is to be left. Because any �subjective� understanding of morals becomes without basis since the human being who defends subjective morals is also distinctly ineffective and reduced to his particles and their behaviors.
While consequences do not show the truth or error of something, we should note in this context as a side effect that the behaviors of sovereign wholes may be negatively influenced by physicalist evolutionary world view. If the behaviors of life forms are reducible to particles that behave according to the deterministic or probabilistic �laws� of physics, then we do not have free will power, reason, and we must not punish people or more generally make people responsible, blamable and praisable. If we reduce things to smaller things then there cannot be consciousness, conscience, and morals.

9. Laws Related to Life Forms
Certain relationships are not reducible ontologically and epistemologically to physical and material relations. 
To critique physicalist evolution based on laws, it is not necessary only that there are laws directly related to physicalist evolution. If what physicalist evolution claims to explain has laws, then physicalist evolution can be criticized based on those laws as well. Hence physicalist evolution can be criticized for having no evidence to reduce the laws or patterns related to economics, psychology, commercial and criminal laws... to the ambiguous laws and patterns related to physics or ASBEs. Such laws do not need to be exact laws like those of physics; for instance regarding indifference curves in economics free will power is important: an economic agent may be indifferent in choosing between a combination of two goods, and another combination of those goods although according to the laws of physics, he has no such indifference and any set of circumstances coercively leads to another physical state. 
In the realm of physics, the distinction between different aggregates such as a banknote or another paper with the same properties is insignificant. However, when it comes to economics and finance, the perspective changes. Even a bullion of aluminum is subjected to distinct analyses in the fields of physics and economics. When human beings are considered as aggregates, physics studies aspects like the heat produced or the force exerted upon their bones when falling from a certain height. It is true that every human being will react similarly to a banknote, but any variations in their reactions are primarily influenced by their circumstances as human beings, rather than minute differences in weight. If free will is distinctly effective, the perception of the value of money and related pleasure is additionally distinctly effective. Similarly, every parent interacts with their child as a human being, recognizing their unique qualities rather than treating them as mere aggregates. The law distinguishes between a human being and a rock, even if they share the same weight. Furthermore, two human beings may exhibit different behaviors based on their citizenship in different countries, despite having the same physical properties as aggregates. These examples highlight that certain sciences, such as economics, finance, and human behavior, and related behaviors at related layers cannot be reduced solely to the physics and behaviors of matter, as they encompass distinct dimensions and considerations that go beyond the physical realm.
Moreover, while the above are specific to life forms, there are also patterns related to life forms as well as to other things. For example, the patterns or laws related to the matter such as laws of motion or inertia are also like the laws, patterns, or relations related to economics. Again, in a final analysis, the problems related to patterns or laws related to motion are not less than those related to consciousness. Like consciousness, the laws related to motion also lead to transcendent unity, other properties of God and irreducibility. They cannot be considered as brute facts since a brute fact would have no properties. Motion of parts can give rise neither to an aggregate, nor to a (holistic) whole. Moving parts are also (holistic) wholes, because of movement and because of movement's indispensable inherent relation with other things. Motion also relates to the entire whole: if an atom moves, it moves relatively to all objects in its universe. Likewise a change in an aggregate of clips happens also as a whole in any case. And what holds an aggregate together and cause reaction to an effect which would dissolve the aggregate is omitted in physicalist evolution. Consciousness is also like this. Therefore in none of them reductionism works, and movement and spatiotemporal relations, patterns, and laws also invalidate reductive aspect of physicalist evolution.
Movement of the matter entails transcendence also in another way: For any moving particles/ waves, a complete knowledge about them would include their positions as of now plus what position they would have in a future time t. Without any future state, we cannot define their movement hence them as of �now�. But if we try to detect now and if now is real as not containing any �future as a future�, then either they contain the future in another form prior to the actualization of the future, or they create the future, or they take their directions from another source.

10. Purposefulness: E.g. Survival
Physicalist evolution undermines the property of purposefulness in living beings, as it abolishes free will, reason, and identity. Hence, it undermines itself as well since one of its key arguments is the survival of the fittest and the struggle "for" survival. Likewise, targeting well-being and avoiding suffering become inconsequential if living beings are reducible to the collisions and movements of particles, waves, and fields. Again, the designing activities of many life forms, including humans, to attain certain purposes are also undermined by the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution. Moreover, according to the physicalist evolution, it is impossible to recognize the �ought to be� property of many types of actions, events, and states.

If not, then physicalist evolution is not possible because then its reductive aspect becomes false since to have free will power hence to run away from a predator in order to survive entails that that life form is not reducible to the fundamental particles. The same applies to consciousness: if we did not suffer would we run away from the tiger? No, our particles would continue existing and furthermore, if a non-unified state of particles would be more enjoyable, then it might be better to be eaten by a tiger.
Also consider the example of hunger. When a person is hungry, they try to alleviate their hunger. If hunger did not exist, they would not behave in such a way. If they did while hunger did not exist, there would be no need for hunger, and hunger would disappear through evolution since the perception of hunger also requires consuming some energy since that perception requires certain signals and physiological processes. This example illustrates how physicalist evolution fails to account for the property of purposefulness behind certain behaviors, rendering them insignificant.
In scenario 1 examined earlier where mechanistic relations at life related layers are recognized as opposed to random ones, we cannot have a perfect circle unless there is transcendence between the ASBEs. The existence of a perfect circle requires transcendence between the entities involved. However, in this scenario, the idea that anticipating the future consequences of encountering a lion (such as potential harm or orphaned children) is illusory. The idea "if I am caught by the lion I will be dead or injured or my kids will be orphans so let me stay away from the lion" is an illusion.  There is no transcendence of the future; atoms and molecules simply behave according to the laws of physics, and there is just that illusion of purposefulness.
For instance, when an iguana looks upwards to scan for predators or a lizard turns its eyes right and left to detect prey, their behaviors do not happen only because their particles move in such a direction that their eyes look like searching a predator or prey. Do their eyes roll because their particles follow their trajectories according to their states right after the big bang, or do they roll up because the iguana wants to survive? The reductive aspect of physicalist evolution fails to account for the purposeful actions of organisms in their quest for survival.
Only God-fashioned evolution sustained by a transcendent being may use the whole-related properties of the holistic units of evolution. For example, under physicalist evolution, there is no effective survival because the ASBEs are the only sufficiently distinctly effective, and the species are only an appearance of the trajectories of ASBEs. However, purposefulness is a key property for the holistic units of evolution. The same applies to concepts like "fitness," "gene," and other holistic aspects related to life.

Reductionist explanations cannot account for the complexities of organisms and their purposeful behavior. The existence of purposefulness and transcendence beyond the ASBEs refutes the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution. The interdependence of wholes and their constituent parts undermines the notion of determining a previous distribution based on a future distribution of parts.

Being closer in space is not defined as something which changes the nature of things being different other than being closer. Even if a new property would be arising from parts that come together, then that new property would be predictable based on the properties of parts hence the whole would not have a distinct effectiveness and therefore only ASBEs would be effective hence physicalist evolution would be just a change in spatial positions as explained in earlier parts without justifying the distinct life layer things. In that case, physicalist evolution would not be the evolution of wholes, but movements of parts.
Transcendence related things (like economy or free will power) at a certain layer cannot be explained by non transcendent things (like movement which allegedly is not transcendent) at another layer even if we use the term �emergent property�. 
The shortcomings of non-reductive physicalism examined in part 1.1.2.2.10 sheds further light on this issue.
