3. Randomness Would not Arise for Free
Physicalist evolution which focuses on random mutations presupposes that the random mutations would occur in any case for free and unquestionably. However, there are lots of requirements like mass, energy, space, time�, so that random mutations may occur. For further details see part 1.4.2.1.1.4.2.1.4 under partial fine tuning. 
Coincidence is not an explanation because in order for coincidence to happen there is a need for the power that produces it. This power is not separable from coinciding factors. The act of throwing the dice also entails such a coincidence as it entails the power to throw. Coincidence cannot explain the result, because it needs that which it allegedly explains. If we cannot toss the dice we cannot talk of a coincidence. The act of tossing requires the unity that is shown in the result. Also in order for the trajectory of the dice to happen, there is a need for energy which unfolds in a specific way. Whatever is the origin of this energy, it acts at any deepest level as a multipotential cause. 
Power cannot be exercised randomly: because it entails causing a change in a specific direction instead of another direction. If the thing that exercises this power does not transcend the multiple directions, then it is not free to take that direction. This entails that it is caused unipotentially by another cause. But then either there will be infinite regress or the real cause will be free to determine the direction.
Can we say that something has a 50 percent probability of existing and 50 percent probability of not-existing if there is nothing which makes it exist? Obviously, �nothing� cannot cause anything, since, if it causes something, then it is not �nothing�.
4. If Randomness is at the Foundation of Physicalist Evolution, Then Physicalist Evolution Collapses.
Is randomness in physicalist evolution a true uncertainty or does it mean unpredictability because of lack of information? Had we known all about the positions, momenta, speed and other physical properties of all particles right after the big bang, could we predict the rise of human beings? If yes, then the unfolding or unfoldable trajectories of all life forms would be existing at right after the big bang, and this would invalidate a true effectiveness of physicalist evolution through time. If no and if there is a true uncertainty, then coming with a theory no matter what it is would be giving us no prediction, since there would be unpredictability at the foundation of particles.
If a certain process of physicalist evolution is random this means that it might not happen. This undermines the predictive aspect of physicalist evolution. If by contrast that process is necessary, then it is necessitated by a previous event or an alleged law. In this understanding of necessity, either there is infinite regress since our observations show us that things in the limited universe depend on other things, or the allegedly random processes of physicalist evolution are necessitated by other events, hence they are not random. Hence, it is not possible to have a consistent place for randomness within the physicalist evolution.  Consequently, the entire whole is neither necessary nor random, it is built on a will and design.
We can conceive of states of billiard balls where under certain assumptions some aggregates may cause orderly/ complex aggregates which arise through some predictable ways within essentially random set of numerous billiard balls. For example a mold like aggregate may cause aluminum profile-like sets of aggregates if there is a specific essentially random distribution of moving balls which can be explained by the big number of balls. If we have enough balls we cannot say any distribution in which there are such relations is impossible. But will this be called physicalist evolution? If randomness is a fundamental part of physicalist evolution, then it must be physicalist evolution. But then, it would not be consistent to expect predictions based on evolution, and it would not be consistent to define evolutionary processes and patterns.
If numerous billiard balls behaved such that some regions or universes had evolving species, would it be evolution? If yes, then there is no tracing of any knowledge back to the fundamental structure of the matter or to the fundamental reality, hence any prediction we make will not be systematically grounded in the fundamental reality. Again, if yes then physicalist evolution is not science or if it is science then science and physicalist evolution have no true predictability linked to the foundation of the universe, it is totally contingent like the willed things by God, but the latter has a connection to ultimate reality and a sovereign whole created by God is real and can justify predictable systems related to the potential purposefulness. But any being or thing allegedly explained by science is arbitrarily defined and delimited, the only effective being, that is the ASBE is impossible as explained in earlier parts. Again, if yes, then, the claims of physicalist evolution regarding absence of God become unfalsifiable, since no matter what complexity we had, physicalist evolutionist might propose the physicalist evolution as an alternative?
If at the initial state of the universe there was entities and the events that would deterministically unfold in the rise of human beings, what was the probability of the rise of human beings and other beings and species? If we presuppose a patterned universe, there will be constraints against probabilities and randomness; if we presuppose an unpatterned universe, then there will be no constraints but probability will again be lower because of the disorder.  
On the other hand, if we presuppose a fundamental randomness, then for each universe that will allow the evolution of certain species like the species of human beings, we can conceive of infinite sets each of which contain infinite number of states which will unfold into a universe that will not allow the evolution of those species. Hence the probability of a universe which will unfold in the evolution of human beings is zero.
5. Indeterministic Events Would Rather Destroy the Accumulated Improvements Instead of Building New Improvements.
While a fully deterministic universe would disprove physicalist evolution as explained above, a fully indeterministic universe would disprove it as well. Likewise, a universe which consists of a combination of both will also be incompatible with a physicalist evolution. 
Indeterminism undermines indeterminism at the very beginning. Because under it there will be no stable whole, since a part may disappear or change direction unpredictably making the whole unharmonized and unmanageable by the brain hence preventing the development of any coherent systems.
If there were no patterns in the limited universe, then could there be life? If parts of the carbon or oxygen atoms behaved in a different way every second or every year, then could we have life forms? If the earth moved a certain way one year and another way another year would we have life forms? 
Furthermore, elements of an unbiased and all-encompassing indeterminism would be destructive for evolution rather than creative, since any gain through millions of years might be destroyed with some indeterministic events, while an indeterministic event would not compensate that destruction by bringing together many precise elements that the organization of life forms need; and the destructive effect of indeterminism would be much bigger than any of its allegedly creative effects.
Mutations result generally in loss of information. If we put aside epigenetics, activation switches and the activation of already existing genes or gene sets which enable certain features, and if we grant that a stable basis upon which random processes operate somehow exists, to produce a tiny even incomplete organ or feature or systematic set of cells, there must be a happy coincidence like monkeys who type by chance a literary work. 
To gain meaningful information many extremely lucky combinations must produce meaningful connections. But if there is such flexibility and the latter works, then harmful mutations will destroy the species quickly.  
If we set up a universe and  the initial state and vectors of billiard balls at time t0 so that at some stage a song plays at time t2, did we explain the song with the positions and patterns at time t1? If an explanation needs an explanation, is it a good and complete explanation and knowledge if determinism is true? Is it a good explanation if indeterminism is true? If indeterminism is true then there is no explanation because by definition, the indeterministic event does not have a complete cause. 
In physicalist evolution, random events happen exactly where they are needed, and deterministic events happen exactly where they are needed. Neither indeterminism nor determinism is supported by any principle; as we saw above determinism undermines physicalist evolution; likewise, indeterminism undermines it as well.
Physicalist evolution theory presupposes that normally random mutations may occur as advantageous mutations and disadvantageous mutations in fundamentally similar likelihoods. 
In the presence of the entropic principles, randomness cannot carry out the function assigned to it by the physicalist evolutionist.
The advantageous ones give the individual the ability to survive by giving the individual additional functions or improvements in existing functions, though sometimes, a diminution in functions may also result in increased survival capacity, like the loss of flying capacity in chicken which then get domesticated and increase in number; and others reduce the ability to survive mostly by additional or improved functions. 
Here, I will omit the mutations which improve functions but which are disadvantageous for survival, and mutations which deteriorate functions but which are advantageous for survival. Because such mutations would not be the cause of the various advanced life forms. And I will rather focus on mutations which allegedly increase new functions or functionality of already existing functions and which in the same time support the survival. These I will call below the advantageous mutations, and the opposite, I will call the destructive mutations.
Mathematically, the likelihood of destructive mutation is more likely unless the mutation is guided. So, normally, the numerous destructive mutations would outnumber in each set of mutations the advantageous ones, and each mutation would be much more intense in its destructive power compared to the beneficial power of the advantageous mutations. If there is a cup on the table but closing your eyes and not seeing the cup you pour juice randomly from a bottle without targeting the cup, it is very likely that you will cause a mess rather than fill the cup.
There may be repair and control systems in place which enhance advantageous mutations; but these systems also would be subject to the increase in entropy.
The materialist might say that since we talk about probabilities, the above considerations cannot be conclusive. But if we know that randomness would essentially cause harm, unless there are some transcendent fundamental systematic biases, we are not justified in saying that random mutations may result in advanced functions overriding the influence of entropy.
If we hit the well-ordered billiard balls, it is very likely that they will have a meaningless distribution, since there are infinitely more potential disorderly distributions compared to orderly and meaningful distributions. If we have written a word with billiard balls, and we strike them randomly, it is likely that the word will be lost. If there is a disorderly distribution of billiard balls and if we strike them randomly, it is very unlikely that they form a word. So, this billiard ball example shows that if the mutations were random, then there would be quick destruction of humanity and anything else. Therefore, randomness may be discarded as a cause of advantageous mutations. 
Is it possible that the structures as in the above billiard ball example exist, but instead of being originated by God, they originated randomly at the initial state of the limited universe? Similar issues raised about randomness above apply in this case, the only difference in this possibility would be that the location of randomness has been moved back. Plus, we would then ask: �Today�s randomness might be said to have at least a substance coming from the past and upon which it allegedly arises; but if the randomness was at the root of the very initial state, then what would be causing that randomness?� 
There are disadvantageous mutations, and advantageous mutations. There are much more disorderly states compared to orderly states. Hence, the disadvantageous random mutations would be much higher than the advantageous mutations, unless there is a bias for the advantageous mutations.
Obviously, a common counter-argument will be this: �Even though the increase in entropy is generally true, in some regions of randomly distributed things there may be things which are distributed in an orderly way. So, since the multiverse is a possibility, the above argument is not conclusive.� However, the mutations do not in fact occur within billiard balls; they occur within and thanks to specific atomic and molecular structures which require many conditions and properties. These structures are also subject to the fundamental probabilistic principle underlying 2nd law of thermodynamics. Hence, we cannot take them as granted and build randomness of mutations upon those structures as if these structures are not subject to that principle. If we do not grant to the physicalist evolutionist the structured atoms and molecules, but we want them to build random mutations upon the parts with zero complexity upon which the atoms are allegedly reducible, can they still claim a possibility for the occurrence of stable random mutations? Can we get the mutations if the atoms were as simple as billiard balls? By the way, we should note that even the billiard balls are extremely complex, but for the sake of argument let us omit the basis of this complexity. Clearly, if the atoms were behaving as simply as the billiard balls, we could not have the advantageous mutations; even if we would get things which looked like advantageous mutations, they would not be advantageous mutations, they would have a very narrow scope, and they would be epiphenomenal.
Moreover, the explanations in part 1.1.2.2.2.14 about multiverse show that the largeness of the limited universe does not constitute a reason to explain things with randomness.
So, mere randomness cannot improve anything unless that in which random processes occur are biased toward improvement. 
6. Natural Selection Together With Random Mutations Does not Cause Necessarily More Species Arise, it may Also Cause Species go Extinct or Have Less Advantageous Traits.
If randomness alone cannot move toward improvement or change, then, can it cause the life forms if it is combined with the survival of the fittest? 
Natural selection just prevents the deterioration by harmful mutations. If the beneficial mutations were isolated, even if the badly mutated beings survived, there would be in some regions those with good mutations. Hence natural selection is not a cause for big changes or changes on top of what already happens. It has no additional positive effect on top of the random mutations to produce any new trait. "If the beneficial mutation happens" natural selection protects it by killing the unfit. It does not create a new fit.
In this context, we also have to consider that the survival advantage is a relative concept. A loss of a trait that causes a survival advantage for a specific species may result in the higher survival of another species, and vice versa. Therefore, it is not necessary that the natural selection leads to the rise in the numbers of the individuals of a group of species. So, randomness and natural selection together may cause increase or decrease in the number of the fittest.
For example, a species that has very competitive traits may cause the species surrounding it go extinct and then its own extinction. If a species possesses traits that make it highly competitive and successful in exploiting available resources, it may outcompete other species and deplete those resources. This can eventually lead to a collapse in the population or the ecosystem, which can be detrimental to the very species that was initially successful due to its advantageous traits.
A classic example of this scenario is the case of the red deer (Cervus elaphus) and the Isle of Rum in Scotland. In the early 20th century, the Isle of Rum had a stable population of red deer, with no natural predators and abundant food resources. Over time, natural selection favored larger and stronger stags, as they had a competitive advantage in mating and passing on their genes.
As a result, the population of red deer on the Isle of Rum became dominated by large and powerful stags. These stags were successful in competing for mates and controlling territories, which led to a rapid increase in the population.
However, the population growth was not sustainable in the long term. The large number of red deer consumed a significant amount of vegetation, leading to overgrazing and depletion of food resources. The ecosystem's carrying capacity, which is the maximum number of individuals that an environment can support, was surpassed, and the available food could no longer sustain the growing population.
As a consequence, the red deer population experienced a severe crash. The once-advantageous traits of being large and competitive became detrimental when the resources became scarce. Many deer died due to starvation and malnutrition, and the population declined dramatically.
Another example, is the moa, a group of flightless birds in New Zealand, that possessed advantageous traits such as a lack of natural predators and large size, which allowed them to thrive and exploit available resources. However, their uncontrolled population growth and herbivorous behavior led to significant resource depletion on the islands, causing changes in the ecosystem. The Moa's inability to adapt to these changes and their self-inflicted resource depletion eventually led to their extinction, illustrating an example of a species that went extinct solely due to its advantageous traits causing ecological imbalance,
On the other hand, human beings who had advantageous traits also led to the extinction of many species. Examples include the Passenger Pigeon, hunted to extinction for meat and habitat destruction; the Dodo, a flightless bird on Mauritius eliminated by human hunting and invasive species; the Woolly Mammoth, which disappeared due to human hunting and climate change; the Tasmanian Tiger, killed off by European settlers and diseases; the Western Black Rhinoceros, hunted for its horn and affected by habitat loss; and the Pyrenean Ibex, extinct in 2000 and briefly brought back through cloning. These cases highlight the profound impact humans have had on biodiversity.
Moreover, the survival disadvantage of one individual is likely to be a survival advantage of another individual in a competing situation: if snakes that eat rats lose their smelling and sight, then the rats may have bigger survival advantage even though nobody has any improved functions; moreover, by the deterioration in snakes, the rats may even deteriorate since they will not need to run and be aware of the environment as in the case where there were agile snakes around.  And in the absence of such snakes, fast running will not be an advantage for the fast running rats. Consequently, natural selection is not necessarily accompanied with the rise in the advantageous traits overall, it can be accompanied with loss of total advantageous traits it the total species in a habitat is considered. Hence, loss of functions may be more influential in increasing the number of surviving individual living things if they are considered as one group. So, whether improved functions or deteriorated functions will be survival advantage and for whom is not a law-like process which necessarily leads to advanced species or more numerous species. Whether any new traits allegedly produced by random mutation cause more species depends entirely upon how the environment, the set of different species, and other conditions have been fashioned.
Since the nature would be indifferent as to what species survive, the objective effects of the survival advantage and of the random mutations may also lead to the extinction of already existing species and their functions. 
On the other hand, if extinction of the fittest may offset the survival of the fittest and if the natural selection is not law-like, then there is no evidence that the natural selection causes the rise of new species. The natural selection�s effect if there is any would not be sufficient to cause new species. If it was law-like in causing positive traits and without opposite effects like the extinction effect, then we might say that it may cause new species. But without this, there must be measurable evidence for its causing new species and that it is more influential in that than its deteriorating effect.
If natural selection as a process with random mutations can affect the results in the opposite directions, then it cannot be claimed to have influence in just one direction unless there are circumstances that cause the influence of that process in just one direction. If the result is in one direction but there may be other causes that may have caused the result in a specific direction, it cannot be said that the natural selection caused that event in one direction. Moreover, if a process has the potential to influence in opposite directions, but there has actually been an influence in just one direction, then the structure in which that process is active must have had certain specifications; in other words, that process is not the only influencer toward the result, but also the structure in which it operates is non-separably influential in the result. Also, since the process itself is the result of the setup and since the setup is contingent, ascribing the new species and traits to the natural selection together with random mutation as a final or key explanation is fallacious and false.
7. The Randomness� Effectiveness in Producing Complex Aggregates is Undermined by the Absence of Certain Complex Aggregates Outside Life Forms
Another necessary component of physicalist evolution along with randomness, is the deep time that increases the probability of complex systems in a life form. These two together with the chemicals constitute also the sufficient elements of physicalist evolution as well: If we have the chemicals present in our world, the random mutations, and the deep time, then we can have the complex life forms. Then we can ask why did not the aircraft arise randomly, if physicalist evolution may happen fully randomly or fully in a naturally selected way. Billions of years passed on earth (deep time), do we see around any boeing 777 having randomly formed? At least a chopper? At least a bike?
The counter argument to this line of thought would be: �The rise of life forms is not necessary when the necessary or sufficient elements of physicalist evolution are present, likewise, the rise of boeing 777 is not necessary. So, likewise, physicalist evolution may happen or may not happen, as boeing 777 may happen or may not happen. Hence, the whole of physicalist evolution is random and contingent. It does not happen necessarily. Similarly, the pathways of physicalist evolution also might have happened, and might not have happened. The happening of life forms does not entail the formation of boeing 777, hence, the non-existence of boeing 777 does not work against physicalist evolution.� However, the actual situation is that the pathways of the life forms and human beings arose randomly through the deep time fully like the random formation of a horse shape in the clouds, but boeing 777 and its pathways have not happened fully or partially like the horse shape in the clouds. But if the entire processes at the reduction basis are random, since a partial randomness does not work as explained above, and if the deep time allowed them to coincidentally come together to form the complex life forms and their pathways, then we are entitled to ask reasonably why a boeing 777 or at least a bike has not arisen randomly.
Physicalist evolution built upon pervasive randomness has no good answer to this question.
8. Random Aspect of Physicalist Evolution Entails That There is no Reasonable Maximally Complex System That Cannot Arise Randomly.
If we develop a technology that can only be 'designed' by transcendent being and not by random events, would this disprove physicalist evolution? Because if physicalist evolution is true, then this technology must have arisen through randomness -since human beings and their abilities are allegedly the result of random events of physicalist evolution-, but if there can be such a technology, then it will be shown that it cannot arise through randomness; so, according to physicalist evolution there is no technology which cannot arise through randomness. If there can be a technology that is impossible to arise through randomness, and if the human beings can do it, then if human beings produce that technology, it will not have arisen through randomness. So, either such a technology is possible by human beings and the human beings are not the result of random evolution, or such a technology is impossible hence any sophisticated technology can arise -only- through randomness. However, we can imagine easily a technology so sophisticated that it cannot arise randomly -at least according to probability calculations-. If it is actualizable when the reasonable sufficient materials are available, even if they are not available as of now, such a correctly devised technology will debunk the physicalist evolution. So, also any kind of material must be able to exist randomly, because if we can conceive a material randomly, then since it can be conceived randomly, it must also be able to exist randomly. Or is the truth that there cannot be such a technology, so according to physicalist evolution all reasonably imaginable technologies may arise randomly? Is it in any case reducible to particles' movements?
9. If Something can Appear Randomly, it can Also Disappear Randomly
If something, some order, some distribution, some substance may appear randomly, then it may also disappear randomly. Either such things, orders, distributions have the power to behave, come into existence randomly, or there is a power which makes them appear randomly. If things may be distributed in a certain way randomly, then they can also be distributed in another way randomly; hence, the first distribution will have disappeared randomly.
If there are such random powers, and if evolution depends on them, then, physicalist evolution will have undermined its own reliability and predictability. Because such randomness may change all. 
If a function of a life form appeared randomly, then it might also disappear randomly. Such randomness would not mean evolution.
10. A Physicalist Evolution Built on Indeterminism Could not be an Argument Against the Fashioning by Allah.
A successful performance which might be a failure can always be claimed to have happened by chance. If a cook cooked a delicious cake, someone may say that he did it by chance; if he cooked one thousand delicious pizzas, again someone may say that he cooked them by chance. Obviously, for a materialist, any perfect cook cooks really by chance since any cook happened to exist by chance through random mutations, and when he cooks, his blind particles are at work randomly. Similarly, for the materialist whatever God creates, such as numerous atoms of different and similar kinds, electrons, cells, DNAs� all of them happen by chance. There is no way to prove for him that any kind of limited universe or life form may have happened through fashioning. Hence, this claim of the materialist is unfalsifiable and arbitrary. Physicalist evolution is an extension of this approach.
If evolution is a holistic process, if in it there are mechanisms like goals to survive, selection of the better, which in and of itself produce changes in species, then indeterminism cannot be true as it relates to evolution.
When there are mutations for each baby, is each mutation random, or do they move toward a certain direction, or are they under some overall or ad hoc control? If things are random, how can we know that they are not in fact guided? There is no way to distinguish something random from something guided in favor of randomness. Random means in this context, that which is without definite aim, direction, rule, or method147. So, we do not know such an aim, but this does not mean that there is no aim for the mutation. Hence, there is nothing to say against the guidance of Allah for anything we see as random. On the contrary, even if we made sure that something is random meaning that it does not have a cause within the limited universe, this means that there is a cause of a different kind, irreducible to the spatiotemporal, since nothingness cannot cause anything.
11. Even if Indeterminism Would be True, Then There had to be a Right Balance Between it and an Alleged Determinism.
Let us recall that if everything at the layers underlying physicalist evolution were fully deterministic, then evolution would have no distinct effectiveness. Some argue that there is some uncertainty within the fabric of the limited universe and that this gives a range of freedom such as free will power to for instance human beings in the layer of life; and that this way the distinctness of life forms and evolutionary processes may be saved. 
As I argued in Tosun, 2020, such an uncertainty cannot give that range of freedom; it cannot produce the distinctness the evolution needs either. However, if we grant such benefits to evolution from uncertainty, then there appears two issues: 
(1) The need for balance between determinism and indeterminism: if all was indeterministic, then there would be a chaos which would undermine physicalist evolution. Yet, if all was deterministic, then there would not be any distinctness of physicalist evolution; hence, it would be just epiphenomenal.
(2) The need for delineation of the borderline between determinism and indeterminism: Let us imagine that there are particles which are deterministic and particles which are indeterministic. Would the deterministic ones be consisting of infinitesimal parts which are deterministic? Would the indeterministic ones be consisting of infinitesimal parts which are indeterministic? Why would not those infinitesimal parts get mixed? If they got mixed, would not this mixture make the particles that we know such as atoms indeterministic, hence chaotic? Would not those deterministic and indeterministic infinitesimal parts have common origin, like ASBEs? Yet, if the parts were the same but in some contexts they would behave deterministically and in others indeterministically, would there be laws that would determine when they would behave deterministically and when they would behave indeterministically? Why would the indeterministic ones obey such laws?
Obviously, we can multiply the questions. And in any case, the answers will lead us to conclude that an alleged balance between deterministic and indeterministic behaviors which would be necessary (but not sufficient) for an allegedly physicalist evolution, would entail the act of a higher power. But since I argue that indeterminism would not be instrumental for giving any distinct effectiveness to the alleged physicalist evolutionary entities and processes, I will not multiply those questions further here.
So, a coexistence of determinism and indeterminism if true, would require further balanced and specified relations irreducible to the spatiotemporal, hence, would prove further the Fashioning Property of the Self-Sufficient Cause.
12. The Randomness Element of Physicalist Evolution Contradicts its Reductive Aspect 
If evolution depends on lower layers that we do not know, then it cannot be claimed to be random unless we demonstrate the randomness at the lower layers.
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.9 An Explanation Based on Fortunate Coincidence Cannot Justify Physicalist Evolution
The recognition and utilization of both holistic elements and their reduction to atoms, molecules, and so on by physicalist evolution is not empirically and mathematically implausible due to its low probability, but also logically contradictory.
From a physics perspective, to explain the positions of particles within life forms, we go to the time where there was no life, and if physicalist evolution is true, then we can see that the only cause for the coming together in a special distribution of the atoms or rather subatomic particles within that body is the trajectories of the particles. Hence, since this would be sufficient for the explanation of the color of the polar bears, the bear and its behaviors used by physicalist evolution must have overlapped with the trajectories of the particles only coincidentally and no evolutionary mechanism at the life layer may have helped their rise. The black bear white bear implications, such as the black bear being noticed by its prey and going extinct as opposed to the white bear, are just a lucky coincidence without having anything to do with any event at the layer of the bear or its prey. So does this make it an issue of probability? No. Though it aggravates the issue of probability, it renders physicalist evolution ineffective and only a fortunate coincidence in principle, that only supports the appearance of evolutionary mechanisms. The fortunate chance does not explain the rise of the complex systems, but only the overlapping of the appearance of those systems with the ongoing trajectories of the particles. Hence, physicalist evolution is unlike a commonly understood branch of science that makes sequential predictions based on the states related to its scope.
If we use the multiverse to explain randomness-based evolution, then all the processes ascribed to physicalist evolution at the life layer collapse again because of the reductive aspect. Because according to randomness based physicalist evolution, the key contribution of the multiverse would be increasing the chance of the overlapping between what appears to be happening to us and the unrelated trajectories of the things at the reduction basis layer.
Even if we saw in the laboratory that atoms coincidentally formed a cell, a method based on physicalist evolution would debunk physicalist evolution itself. However, we should note that the method of some apologetics such as Stephen Meyer would concede that at least at a certain level God is not necessarily involved with life. They use the low probabilities as the key counterargument against physicalist evolution. They recognize the atheistic claim that the background is self sufficient once the big bang happened.
This approach focuses on probabilities and assumes that once the low probability sequence, structure, and life arising from non life happened, then the physicalist evolution would be fine.  This is a consequence of the contemporary mainstream Christian/ Jewish teaching that god can rest or die or become human and that the universe can go on while god is dead or takes rest or keeps being a human.
If the formation of a cell is a matter of probability, then the existence of God also becomes a matter of probability as well; because this entails that the fabric or raw material of the first cell exists or may exist without needing God. The need for God for the big bang is also quite weak if the matter can keep existing once it was created at the big bang, because it assumes that at present, the matter has the capacity to keep its existence no matter whether it was given by God or by another thing. However, if God is assumed to be matter-like or human-like, then the need for something other than the matter becomes weaker. Then no matter how small the likelihood of the formation of the first cell is, the physicalist evolutionist may say that the matter-like God may have a smaller likelihood of being and  that the small likelihood of the formation of the first cell may be greater than that of God.
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.10 Physicalist Evolution is Partial and Incomplete.
Physicalist evolution theory considers only some parts of our observations and does not consider sufficiently the implications related to the physics upon which it depends: it takes as given what physics say. But contradictorily, it claims that evolution is reducible to physics. It does not consider sufficiently all of the human observations such as consciousness.
If physicalist evolution is only about changes in spatial distribution and suspends judgment about consciousness, reason, free will power, knowledge, beauty, love, then it is not a qualified competitor nor a qualified substitute of fashioning. Because in this case, these facts which are essential for fashioning may only be originated by an ultimate cause who has these properties. 
But if it claims that these properties are reducible to the movement of particles, then it will have undermined its rationality as explained in part 1.1.2.2.3.10. 
Physicalist evolution is not the only way to improve life forms. As the guidance of Allah is possible through the allegedly random mutations, according to the alleged empirical and logical tools of physicalist evolution, it is totally possible that life is produced by an intelligent being. 
Physicalist evolution theory does not rule out simulation theory either. According to physicalist evolution, the allegedly ongoing evolution may also be conducted by intelligence and there is nothing contradictory in it, if the properties like consciousness, free will power are reducible to the spatiotemporal. So, when someone presents physicalist evolution as an argument against God, he is not being consistent within his reasoning. 
The use of physicalist evolution against the Fashioner property of Allah is partial and incomplete. To use it against fashioning one needs to prove that the facts supporting physicalist evolution cancels out the possibility of the creation of life forms by a Fashioner. But they cannot do this. Yet they can argue that fashioning is not demonstrated by life because life �may� also be caused by physicalist evolution processes, instead of a Fashioner. This is only reasonable if the Fashioner needs the row materials that the evolution needs as well such as the physical particles and if He cannot create them. But if physicalist evolution by its definition needs the atoms and so on, but if the Fashioner by His properties observed in the limited universe is able to create those particles and so on, then evolution is not an alternative to the Fashioner, because it cannot create and fashion the row materials, while the Fashioner can. So, even at the level of definitions and properties, physicalist evolution is no competitor against the Fashioner, and its properties are insufficient to make it a substitute instead of Allah.
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.11 Physicalist Evolution Could Only be an Approximation
In our context, when we reduce a thing x to another thing y, while x is different than y, this is an approximation. For example, if I make an approximate circle by using ten spoons, and ask a person P �what shape it is�, while P looks from far and cannot see the details of that shape, he may say that it is �a circle�. When he says this, he misrepresents both the spoons and the circle: the spoons may be more like a decagon from a closer distance; yet it is not exactly a decagon either, because, the spoons have curvatures and so on. Likewise, a circle is a geometrical shape. It has perfect mathematical properties. Maybe there is no actual object(s) which constitute a perfect circle. If P believes that he is just making an approximation, since he does not have sufficient access to what constitutes that circle, then he is being rational. However, if he believes that �that circle� has effects as a circle in and of itself, then he is committing an error. This is like the error that the physicalist evolutionist commits: 
The physicalist evolutionist recognizes that the life forms have certain features such as survival motivation; that they have certain processes such as reproduction. However, if they are reducible to atoms and other particles, then there are just the behaviors of the atoms in accordance with the laws of physics. Regarding the spoon example, if reductiveness of evolution is true, then there are just the atoms which correspond to the spoons, and there are no life forms and properties like consciousness which correspond to the �circle� and the features of circle respectively. However, if reductiveness of evolution is false, then the distinctly effective properties of the distinct individual life forms are true. Hence, for reasons explained in part 1.5.2.2.3.3, the distinctly effective properties of life forms are true; hence, the reductive aspect of evolution is false. For the same reason, the implicit claim of the physicalist evolution that the life forms are approximations is false. Therefore, it is also contradictory, for claiming that the approximations have distinct dynamics such as the survival of the fittest.
In parallel with the above, when the physicalist evolutionist says that the fit survives, this means that the positions of particles (such as atoms) which look like a fit life form in our layer will last longer. Here, the physicalist evolutionist is like the person in the spoon example who identifies the spoons as a circle. The physicalist evolutionist believes that an atom will always behave in the same way, ceteris paribus, no matter what shape it constitutes, like a spoon which will behave in the same way, ceteris paribus, no matter what shape it constitutes. The circle, is just an appearance of the spoons from a specific point of view; that circle is not the ontological essence of the spoons which may cause infinite appearances from infinite angles and distances.
If the life forms are just an appearance and approximation of a concrete ontological reality but not distinctly and effectively that reality, then the predictions based on those appearances will have little value. Because, it is impossible to have a sufficient understanding based on appearances. Moreover, being led by appearances, may cause errors: the person who sees the spoons and thinks that he sees a circle, may think that it is a circular object. He may think that this is a bike-wheel. And he may ascribe to what he perceives properties that the spoons do not have. 
While the spoons are one ontological reality in this example, the concept of a circle is also a different ontological reality since using perfect circles, which maybe never occur as an object in the limited universe. The approximation the person makes misrepresents the spoons, however, accepting a circle only as an approximation also misrepresents the concept of the circle, like the transcendent mental powers of the human being and other beings are misrepresented in physicalist evolution. As in free will power brain observation experiment in part 1.6.2.1.1.3, which shows irreducible free will power, we can conceive of perfect circles which maybe do not exist in the physical world and which are not reducible to the particles, yet which are effectively, distinctly useful, and ontologically real tools. And we can even compare accidentally appearing imperfect circles in the actual world to perfect circles, and take related decisions which affect the spatiotemporal world thanks to our irreducible transcendence.
As the physicalist evolutionist considers the life forms as one appearance of particles, when he identifies a pattern based on the appearances, this pattern is ontologically a pattern of the particles. So, what he does according to physicalist evolution theory, is to infer the behavior and nature of particles based on their appearances. Hence, the physicalist evolutionist does not try to identify in fact the properties and behavior of the life forms, and he does not recognize such irreducible, distinct, and effective properties. 
Hence, it might be better to consider physicalist evolution under physics. If the human beings had a nature which is totally different than and disconnected from the living world, we might consider the life forms like robots, and we might consider biology as a branch of physics. But, as we are closely related to and intertwined with the living world, we know for sure by experience, introspection, and observation that the life forms do not consist of things which have only spatial extension and differentiation. Other things also have transcendent properties like free will power, knowledge, reasoning power, consciousness. In this respect, the similarity of human beings to some other life forms and similarities between many life forms is quite wise as an aspect of God�s creation.
On the other hand, one might argue that the physics and chemistry also use approximations since atoms or electrons are not the bottom elements, hence from a reductive point of view, they should be approximations built on the ASBEs. If physicalist evolution studies a certain appearance of atoms, physics which studies the atoms is studying some appearances of more fundamental particles that it does not know yet. However, physics deals with spatiotemporal change; and when studying atoms, electrons, and so on, physics does not declare opinions on whether they do have reasoning power, consciousness, and so on; hence, the reductive physicist may claim that he is not denying some obvious properties. The properties that he studies is common within the scope of his study. He may claim that he is studying at least the spatiotemporal things and relations as effective things, since, even if atoms, electrons� are reducible to and approximations of ASBEs, the features of atoms, electrons� will give information of the same kind as that of the ASBEs. So, he can claim that he is studying effective things, and therefore this study may be useful.
We may use an analogy about psychology in this respect: The statement �psychology interacts with physics� is very different than the statement �psychology is no more than physics�. In order to say the latter, one has to have a sufficient grasp of both. If we cannot fully predict psychology based on physics and give a full explanation for their differences, then we are not entitled to say that psychology is no more than physics.
Accepting that physicalist evolution is an approximation, is admitting that it is partial, limited and incorrect, and that its study of its core subject matter which is the life, will never give us a correct and even partial understanding of distinctly effective things and properties at the layer of life; and that since it does not study a being, an entity, or a property which is distinctly effective, it will never contribute to physics which is the main branch of science which allegedly studies the core of what is underlying evolution from all respects it can. The correct approach should be that the things within the realm of life have their distinct properties and effects; hence, they should not be considered as approximations but as irreducible wholes, which produce additional value on top of the knowledge we get from physics and help us progress in reaching higher degrees of knowledge. The biology may better contribute to an unlimited and undogmatic science in this way. 
Consequently, the use of an approximation by physicalist evolution is false, since it reduces irreducible properties and effects. 
Let us also analyze the issue further based on the clips analogy explained in part 1.4.2.2.8.5.1.2.12. Let us now suppose that some clips which got intertwined constituted a ball. The ball does not change how the clips behave. A clip�s structure contains how it will behave under which circumstances. When they constitute a ball, there is zero change in each clip�s essential structure. Is a new spatiotemporal positioning of the clips a new whole? If I say, when the ball gets bigger than a certain size, it breaks down into two balls, my explanation,  in parallel with the physicalist evolution, is not and cannot be a complete and distinct one based on the size of the ball, but based on the properties of the clips. If a clip breaks under a specific strain, this is what determines the supervenient/ reducible behavior of the ball which the clips constitute. When we say ball, unless it has an irreducible feature, it is a restatement of the spatiotemporal� positioning and other conditions of the clips. The observed relations of the ball may give some true knowledge about the clips. But the issue is whether we accept that the ball has any distinct effect and being or not.  If the ball gives no additional true knowledge on top of the complete knowledge we can get from the clips, and if it has no distinct effectiveness, then it is just a rewording of a group of clips. But if it has a distinct existence, our study of the ball in and of itself may give at least some information that is impossible to get by the study of the clips. In the latter case, we accept that there is another cause for the existence and behavior of the ball other than the clips; and that it is a sustained distinct whole. 
On the other hand, note that the same considerations about the ball applies for the clips, since a clip would also have parts. There cannot be two separate workings at two layers under reductionism; because the opposite entails transcendence where the whole of the ball transcends its parts, communicates, and cooperates with the wholes of its parts. Once this transcendence is admitted, then there is no reason against the transcendence of Allah, since one layer cannot be the result of the other layer, and parts cannot define each other in a circularity.
In physicalist evolution, a bird chirping to attract a mate is more likely to spread its genes whereby in the following generations there will be better chirping birds. The seeming motivation to spread its genes is no more than a random part of the behaviors of the bird�s particles through many years; the genes also are approximations; the essential would be points and point-to-point relations. But then what would �point� and �point-to-point relation� mean? Points also would be defined by each point�s relation to other points. Hence, in any case, there would be transcendence and unity. In determinism and indeterminism, hence, in reductive physicalism, the particles behave without being influenced by what is going on at the layer of birds.
In physicalist evolution, there is no distinctly effective new species on top of the ASBEs. Species is just a repositioning of ASBEs. The only effective things are ASBEs. But for evolution there must be functional ASBEs at the beginning. ASBEs always behave as they have to. Under any specific condition, they would have to change in the corresponding same way to produce complex structures; but then they would not be ASBEs. Because to produce complex organisms, they have to have a minimum complex structure. So, they must have more fundamental parts. Or they must be assumed to be fashioned. If more fundamental parts get combined to form ASBEs. then these more fundamental parts will be complex hence must be fashioned as well.
If the universe is deterministic, then there is no power at the life layer, to adjust freely for new circumstances. If a gazelle runs away from the lion this running away must be entailed by the deterministic initial state. The gazelle does not have transcendent power to adjust its state if it sees a lion. If the gazelle is running away from the lion, it is not running away to save itself, or to avoid pain, or to save its genes; it just looks like it is doing those things, but in fact, its particles continue bumping each other as a continuation of the events at the big bang. To us, these bumps and trajectories look like a gazelle which tries to save itself. Physicalist evolution tells us that if we were able to measure and comprehend all behaviors of particles, we would clearly see that the patterns of the particles would be sufficient to explain the behavior of the aggregate of the gazelle without reference to any �fear�, �pain�, �identity�, �consciousness�, �free will� of the gazelle. 
However, the physicalist evolutionist omits the fact that these bumping relations need to be explained like the behavior of the gazelle needs explanation. Yet, in this case, we have to assume that either the gazelle does not have any consciousness, and qualia like fear, pain, joy, or we have to assume that if reduction is true, the supervenience bases have already the properties of these qualia; if these properties already exist in those supervenience bases, then what has evolved becomes obscure, because, even before the existence of the gazelles, the chemical and physical processes did have the allegedly irreducible elements of such feelings and bases necessary for constituting the aggregates of perceiving, running away, reproduction and so on which would be brought together within the individual life forms.
So, an important problem with physicalist evolution is that it is just an approximation with zero precise real knowledge as its product. The second problem is that it abolishes any value of the distinctness and effectiveness of the human being and his activities, since particles move without taking into account the boundaries of the individual life forms. These human activities  include science which, according to physicalist evolution, becomes a deterministic outcome of the initial state of particles of the universe.
Question 76. 
Is not chemistry also an approximation based on the physical particles and their behaviors? So do the same problems apply to chemistry as well?
Answer 76. 
Chemistry in our contexts concedes that it deals with different aspects of that which is spatiotemporal, of the spatiotemporal positions of things and their differentiations from different angles. When it deals with molecules and chemical reactions, it is not different than the physics in nature. It does not have things like consciousness, ought to be truths, free will power, identities of individuals which �need� to be or which will be reduced to spatiotemporal positions and spatiotemporal extensions. 
However physicalist evolution claims that things evolve, even though it claims that it just deals only with how ASBEs behave under differing conditions. Based on this evolution, it claims that our consciousness, free will power� are nothing more than the bumping of particles; while neither chemistry nor physics makes such a claim against our empirical observations. Physics also concedes that it deals with how ASBEs behave under different conditions. If physicalist evolution also does the same, then it will be saying that the human beings are nothing more than ASBEs behaving under different conditions, and do not have any distinct existence; nor do any other individuals of other life forms.
If physicalist evolution explains only the changes between species through random mutations, then it does not explain the stages before the system of mutations is built, hence, the stages of abiogenesis. But if it does not explain abiogenesis, then even if life came from an original cell, then physicalist evolution would be explaining at best how that cell adapts to differing conditions, it would not be explaining how the systems of that cell rose. If physicalist evolution explains as a chemical evolution the rise of that cell as well, and if there is a smooth transition between the molecular structures, then what happened was that the molecules transformed into other molecular structures; and life is no more than behaviors of molecules. In this case, as explained in part 1.4.2.2.8, physicalist evolution would not be explaining anything different from chemistry and physics.
Question 77. 
The clips might have their distinct behaviors. But if we assume a process as �when they constitute a specific triangle, at the following step they will constitute a strong square�, does not this mean that the triangle is effective as a precursor to that square? So, while the triangle is reducible to the clips and their positions, why would not we consider the triangle as a distinctly effective reality since without which the strong square would not happen? Why would not we consider that transition as a distinct process? Why would not that process be considered as an distinctly effective process just because the initial state of the clips entailed that process and contained already how that process would unfold? 
Answer 77. 
Here if the triangle is distinctly effective, then the clips also would be effective. But if we say (as the physicalist evolution says) that the triangle is not distinctly effective because it is reducible to the clips, and that the clips are distinctly effective then we would be contradicting ourselves; because the clips also consist of parts. Physicalist evolution denies the distinct effectiveness of for example the human beings and their properties, and says that they are reducible to their atoms/ or rather ASBEs, while it recognizes the distinct effectiveness of the ASBEs which are allegedly only spatiotemporal/ material. On the other hand, if the initial state which contains the clips and their laws are recognized as the distinctly effective things, which are active throughout unfolding process, and the unfolding triangle is considered only epiphenomenal, then again the above problem happens, because the ASBEs which exist all along the unfolding are supposed to take the shape of the triangle where the triangle is passive and epiphenomenal. But if the triangle is seen as distinctly effective with certain distinct properties, then it will be recognized as sustained by something other than the clips. Note that if it is assumed to have only the properties like the clips without any distinct additional properties, the clips will not have any superiority over the triangle, because they also consist of parts which produced the shape of clips, and this would go on in an infinite regress as long as parts have extension and if the entire whole of layers are not considered as a whole sustained transcendently. Consequently, the clips also will be recognized as something which is of the same dependent nature as the triangle; hence, we will correctly understand that the clips are also sustained by a sustainer.
So, when we consider the triangle as a distinctly effective reality, ultimately it is not reducible to the clips, and fully explained by the clips, since the clips cannot be the end point. If the clips are supposed to have a totally different and ultimate causal power, then the triangle will be only the act of the clips, hence, it cannot be considered to have any distinct effectiveness.
Furthermore, the above assumes that both the clips and the triangle have only spatiotemporal relations and properties; regarding life, there are irreducible aspects like consciousness and free will power.
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.12 Reductive Aspect of Physicalist Evolution Contradicts the Ontology, Epistemology, and the Raison d�Etre of Physicalist Evolution
Physicalist evolution on one hand recognizes the distinct effectiveness of the life forms and their properties, and on the other, it rejects this effectiveness by claiming that this effectiveness resides within the things at the reduction basis. 
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.12.1 If the Reductive Aspect of Physicalist Evolution is True, Then Physicalist Evolution Collapses Epistemologically and the Explanations as Mutations or Natural Selection are Nonconsequential.
But the bases of those explanations are consequential because things want and struggle to survive. When we trace back and determine the past based on the future states, using physics and chemistry which are the reduction basis of physicalist evolution, there is no process of evolution by which we trace back, predict, and deduce the past; yet the physicalist evolutionist expects the past to be determinable this way.
Physicalist evolution has to ascribe some distinct powers to the things in the life level, else the results of these powers like the motivation to survive will have to have happened and overlapped with the physical trajectories of the particles randomly.
The physicalist evolution needs to recognize the irreducible if it claims to distinctly explain certain events within its scope. 
If physicalist evolution had not recognized the holistic aspects, there would be no bridge between the physical and the life. Then there would be just the collisions and bonds between the particles, and then there would appear the life forms and species. However, physicalist evolution recognizes the distinct effectiveness of events at the layer of life. It needs to recognize the distinct effectiveness because without it, what it claims to explain would be just the changes in spatial distributions of particles and their trajectories. If it rejects the distinct effectiveness of life forms and their life related processes seeing them as epiphenomenal events, then it would be rejecting itself and its own function of explaining the origin of species. Moreover, the production of life forms which would be just specific spatial distributions of particles through collisions would not be convincing explanations at all. 
Chemistry, unlike physicalist evolution, kind of summarizes what happens at the subatomic layers, there is no clear conflict between for instance the nature of what happens at the layer of molecules and at the layer of subatomic particles. But that a gazelle runs away from a lion is something difficult to bridge with collisions and bonds of subatomic particles; that these collisions and bonds with their distinct patterns appear to be like a gazelle is running away from a lion requires extreme creativity in theorizing. The physicalist evolutionist cannot explain something that he rejects. So, to present an explanation of the irreducible, he has to recognize it. But recognizing it normally results in rejecting reductionism. Yet, to undertake the project of reducing the irreducible to the physical, results in a contradictory theory, namely, the physicalist evolution.
This way, the physicalist evolution becomes self-refuting. Because it has to recognize the distinct wholes in order to bring in an explanation about the rise of species. But when it recognizes these, it contradicts its reductive endeavor. 
So, the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution entails that it explains aggregates, not distinct and effective wholes. If reductionism of physicalist evolution is true, then there is the problem of infinite regress and all other problems of reductive physicalism noted in the related parts of this book. But on top of those, its holistic elements also contradict physicalist evolution.  
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.12.2 If Physicalist Evolution Recognizes the Distinct Effectiveness of Life Forms, Mutations, Natural Selection, Holistic Structure Then its Reductive Aspect Collapses.
The previous part entails that the physicalist evolution needs to recognize the distinct effectiveness of the relata, relations, and properties at the life layer. If we use a process at a higher layer as an explanation sincerely, this means that we recognize the distinct effectiveness of the things including those processes at the higher layer. Otherwise physicalist evolution will have contradicted itself, since if the reduction is true, then the real explanation would be at an infinitely lower layer and the process at the higher layer that we use would be no explanation at all. This is important for physicalist evolution. Because if reductive aspect of physicalist evolution is true, it is clear that neither the survival inclination of life forms, nor the random mutation processes are distinctly effective.
If the whole has some distinct effectiveness on top of its constituents then it is not fully reducible onto them. If it does not have that distinct effectiveness, then that upon which it is reduced will have some constituents upon which it is not reducible, since if it is reducible to them in principle, then there will be infinite regress. Hence, the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution is invalidated. Further details that demonstrate this point are given in related parts.
This necessitates the falsity of the reductive aspect of the physicalist evolution. If the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution collapses, then it needs an ultimate cause for its explanations, since they cannot be explained by reduction. 
1.4.2.2.8.5.1.13 Physicalist Evolution is not Scientific
Even though the Islamic method has criteria to test and distinguish that which was fashioned from that which was not fashioned, the reductive physicalism does not have such criteria, and cannot do this distinction. With all of its premises and arguments, the physicalist evolution cannot claim that the limited universe is not fashioned, though it is used as a substitute for Allah. It is used as such a substitute, by making reference to the unknown lower layers and their unknown potentials. So as such a substitute, it is an untestable faith. In any case we can say that we do not know and that we will know later and we can assume to be logical by rejecting the fashioning by claiming ignorance. However in Islam we can know by observing that something is fashioned. Allah observes His fashioning, human beings observe their fashioning, and the requirements of fashioning can be determined. Reductive method may reject anything really fashioned by reference to lower layers' deterministic or indeterministic unknown powers and unquestioned brute facts. According to an unlimited and undogmatic science, fashioning is detectable.
When we determine the means and criteria to distinguish that which is fashioned, then we may conclude that the universe is fashioned.
Physicalist evolution is likewise unscientific and unfalsifiable, by the standards of the limited science. It can allegedly explain the life without reference to fashioning, even if it was fashioned. 
If physicalist evolution is true in its claim that the properties such as consciousness, free will power are reducible to the spatiotemporal, then it would be possible that the universe is a simulation fashioned by intelligent beings with an advanced technology. Yet physicalist evolution would have explained it by reference to unknown lower layers which it considers to be random and not the outcome of fashioning and other transcendent properties. It does not have the means to distinguish whether life is possible to be the outcome of transcendent properties, yet it is used as an argument against God. 
Physicalist evolution is not science. It is ambiguous as opposed to God-fashioned evolution, it is not clear what it is studying. It is a world view. It is incomplete and arbitrary: it makes a claim which according to it, may equally be otherwise. 
The physicalist evolution does not have the power and means to distinguish what is fashioned from what is not fashioned. In other words it is not falsifiable in terms of its criteria. Physicalist evolutionists say that we can distinguish what human beings make by tracing to the factories and so on. But this is not an answer to the question whether the human beings are the result of random processes. We do not know that there are fashioned things by merely tracing things to human beings, since things other than human beings may fashion things if they use the same powers used by human beings in fashioning things. In conjunction with multiverse, in a detailed analysis, physicalist evolution posits something like this: The infinite number of combinations of billiard balls will contain states/ slices where the billiard balls look as if they are evolving species.

However, physicalist evolution makes additional claims: The billiard balls which behave in law-like manners, look randomly as if they are evolving species; and we can make predictions based on the appearance of those billiard balls.

So, the fittest survives would be just an epistemological statement, with zero ontological effect. The society is a whole with the disabled and fittest, and the disabled completes the society in many ways.
4. Physicalist Evolution is not Testable, Measurable, Verifiable, and Repeatable
If Allah creates a new being then the physicalist evolutionist will say it happened randomly, like through random mutation. If a specific molecular or sub-atomic system is required for the existence of life, he will say that such systems happened randomly or it may have happened randomly. 
It presupposes that �things are reducible� to things that we do not know.
Let us remember the analogy of the billiard balls example at the reduction basis layer, and that there the billiard balls sometimes pass through each other and sometimes hit one another. If these produce a seemingly life form in a different layer, we cannot call it evolution because it is not evolving anything, there is no specific thing which evolves. If we call it evolution, then a random behavior will be called evolution and it will be arbitrary and useless in predicting anything; it will not be anything repeatable testable in many higher layers. Likewise each sea wave is unique and unrepeatable, but the movements of atoms may be repeatable if we omit their lower layers. But if we consider the protons, neutrons, and other sub-atomic particles within a reductive approach, then the atoms� behaviors will not be a repeatable behavior, but the details of protons and electrons will be repeatable and they will be disturbing the repeatability of atoms -note that here we omit the infinite regress problem examined in other parts of this book-. However, if we recognize the distinct reality and effectiveness of the things at multiple layers, then, the repeatability of things at multiple layers will enable us to predict to a certain extent the behavior of a whole at a certain layer, and if it is influenced or disturbed by something at another layer, this will not invalidate that repeatability, since an interaction of multiple things does not prevent repeatability in principle. However, note that the repeatability here is not a deterministic repeatability, rather it is a repeatability that results from the repeatable and contingent behaviors of sovereign wholes with respect to their purposes and structures.
The movement of the car is repeatable. But when a part is missing, it is not repeatable. So, we cannot say that a life form is repeatable or any of its behaviors in physicalist evolution: Only the parts behavior will be repeatable if physicalist evolution is true. If we consider chaos theory, then there is almost zero repeatability: A tiny disconnection in the brain of a life form may make it unrepeatable as well; yet what is distinct to the life form may be repeatable under the control of that life form.
If colored billiard balls' evolve into a bird which distinctly affects the balls' movements, then we can measure the effect of evolution. But if all subsequent positions of balls can be predicted by the earlier positions and the movements of balls (that is by the movements of the parts) then the evolution cannot be measured.
If since the big bang physicalist evolution had zero effect on the trajectories of particles, how can we measure and confirm the truth and effectiveness of physicalist evolution? If it had any effect on those trajectories while it is reducible to those trajectories, would not this mean that it is ineffective, since, there would be a circularity, which would mean that the trajectories determine subsequent trajectories and spatiotemporal positions. Therefore, in a physicalist evolutionist framework, the fundamental physical forces determine where every particle is and will be, hence, the truth of physicalist evolution is not detectable and testable.
Again, we should note that a true randomness is not measurable and falsifiable.
If physicalist evolution claims that everything is created through evolution, this is practically an untestable claim. Physicalist evolution builds its claims on the random behavior of molecules. But if it realistically tried to do what is in fact necessary regarding its world view aspects, then it would have to use the ASBEs, because it is reductive and it claims to explain the complex by the simple.

Physics (not reductive physicalism) does not explain how it gets to more complex from the simple, it connects what it gets. If lower layer is more complex, that is fine in physics. If the lower layer is ASBEs then it cannot get from it to life, hence there can be only luck which explains the overlapping. Because supply demand and price relationships have elements totally different from those of billiard balls. So, physicalist evolution looks like it is doing a great job, but in fact it does not. It claims to explain just a part of complexity, but it does it by relocating what it claims to explain into a different branch of science although that branch does not assume the mission of explaining things at the life layer.

If this is true, then physicalist evolution does not add any predictive content on top of the predictions by masses and their spatial distributions, that is on top of the scope of physics.
8. Physicalist Evolution Would be Unpredictive
Even if physicalist evolution predicted anything, it would be according to the background physical events according to the alleged physical laws, not because of alleged dynamics of physicalist evolution; because of physicalist evolution�s reductive aspect.
According to physicalist evolution, and if it is scientific, testable, measurable, and repeatable, then there must be a deterministic or probabilistic predictability. The predictive power attributed to the physicalist evolution works neither with respect to God, nor with respect to what we observe in biology and related sciences: God might equally create life through evolution without any gap in the common ancestry. So physicalist evolution per se does not entail the non-existence of God. Physicalist evolution can never be a substitute for God. On the contrary an evolution is a better indicator of God. A sudden appearance of life forms/species is more probable, than the rise of species through evolution or common ancestry; because the latter scenario requires the fortunate chance of the related processes and pathways at different layers on top of the mere rise of life forms. If a specific car appeared randomly in a world, and in a second world it  appeared randomly again, but in a car factory, then we would say that the latter is more unlikely since the conditions necessary for the car obtained randomly in both worlds, but in the second world on top of that, the conditions of the factory also obtained and the car appeared within that factory. A related example in this context would be this: If there are molds and a foundry and they multiply things, and if there are micro-beings who do not detect them, but who detect only the micro-parts of their universe with their complete knowledge about those micro-parts and their trajectories, they will be able to predict all the trajectories even though they are not aware of the mold and the factory. If the mold and the factory are not distinctly effective, then this situation will correspond to the paradigm of the physicalist evolution. Hence, the mold or the car factory will not add anything to the predictability. So, if the reductive aspect of physicalist evolution is true, then the common ancestry and related things do not have any predictive power or the ability to compete with or replace God.
Let us consider in this context the earlier example of clips that form certain shapes and forms: If we say a four handed clips star will not grow as a law this will not be conclusive. But if we find that a clip cannot support four handed starclips beyond a point and will release then we have found a truer explanation. According to holistic approach even illusions have distinct effects in the limited universe through free will power and consciousness or through consciousness at different layers. While in physicalist evolution these distinct effects do not exist.
If evolution is true, then would it predict that things will change for better? Or can they also change for worse? If still it claims to make predictions, then this means that it recognizes not only change, but also the distinct reality of that which changes or that which does not change.
Hence it is not a scientific hypothesis and it is not scientific. Shall a certain brain structure develop under certain conditions? If such a prediction cannot be made, supposing we have complete knowledge of a past state, then physicalist evolution is not scientific according to normal standards of physicalist evolution.
