(Quran: 5/15-16)
This part analyzes the sustaining property �guidance� that we not only directly experience, but also observe within the limited universe. Like the previous sustaining properties, this property also certainly exists and it is not reducible to the things within the limited universe. 
On the other hand, this part will focus on the guidance through Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the Quran. Although the previous explanations about the previous sustaining properties demonstrate key properties of Allah, this part is especially important in demonstrating that the contents of the Quran are correct as a guidance about the self-sufficient cause of the universe.
1.10.1 Syllogism for the Sustaining Property �Guidance� (SPGU)
O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
By which Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darknesses into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
(Quran: 5/16)
O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
(Quran: 4/174)
The syllogism for the sustaining property �guidance� is as follows.
1. The things in the limited universe entail a self-sufficiently exercised guiding power and the properties entailed by this power. 
2. Things in the limited universe do not have self-sufficiently the guidance property and the properties entailed by it.
3. There is a being above the limited universe, who self-sufficiently has the guidance property and related properties.
1.10.1.1 SPGU Step 1: The Things in the Limited Universe Entail a Self-Sufficiently Exercised Guiding Power and the Properties Entailed by This Power.
This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for the righteous.
(Quran: 2/2)
This premise means that there is a sustaining guidance  property which was and is exercised self-sufficiently. 
Guidance exists. In the following we will see what it is and its types that we observe in different ways. 
Note that at this stage, there is no claim about whether this property belongs to the limited universe or things in it, or to a being beyond the limited universe.
1.10.1.1.1 What is Guidance
The broad definition of guidance is the quality of guiding. The definition of the verb �to guide� is �to direct, supervise, or influence usually to a particular end�207. In our context, guidance of Allah is the power to direct, supervise, or influence to a particular end.
The distinctive and core element of guiding is the intention to at least influence toward an end. This element may be accompanied with an exercise of power that may be in the form of coercively forcing the guided thing toward an end, or in the form of communicating a knowledge like a goal to the guided about the end or about something related to the end in order to influence the guided proceed or progress toward that end. 
The �end� within guidance is not necessarily a new state; it may be a guidance to not do something.
Guidance is related to other sustaining properties explained in part 1.10.1.1.1.
The Quran essentially uses the verb generally in this neutral meaning. For example, the following verse uses the verb �to guide� for influencing toward a bad end:
And of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil.
It has been decreed for every devil that whoever turns to him he will misguide him and will guide him to the punishment of the Blaze.
(Quran: 22/3-4)
We also see in many verses that the target of guidance as a good thing is distinctly clarified instead of using �guide� or �guidance� as a word that alreadly contains the good target. The following verse is such an example:
Guide us in the right path;
(Quran: 1/6)
In the following verse we see the usage of the verb �to guide� as a more general term that relates to even physical events:
(Moses) said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it.
(Quran: 20/50)
So, Allah creates and fashions things, and He also guides them from state to state, or from points to points: Something may be guided from location L1 to location L2 as in the example of the earth rotating around the sun; or from state S1 to state S2 as in the example of a lazy person being guided from laziness to �being hardworking� or a person who hates a neighbor from hatred to loving his neighbor.
This guidance may be of a coercive nature like the creation of the conditions that push things with limited free will to different states, points, or to stay in the same point or state. However, it does not need to be coercive like a coercive exercise of the sustaining power property. It may be in an interaction with the free will of an agent who may be guided as in the following example: 
And as for (the community of) Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn. 
(Quran: 41/17)
In the above verse, Allah does His part of guidance, and provides guidance to the community Thamud. But that community rejected the guidance. So the guidance may have happened but have been rejected. It may be in the form of an option. 
Staying in the same state or point is also a result of guidance of Allah. 
Although guiding things from point or state A to point or state B or stay in the same point relates primarily to the guidance of Allah, it may also overlap in certain ways with His fashioning or creating powers. It may be like the moving parts such that they constitute a machine; yet moving is a different property.
Guidance may essentially happen within a fashioned framework as noted in the above verses. Even the spacetime can be considered as such a framework. Then there is guidance that causes or influences something to transition from being at point a to being at point b. When guidance is in interaction with free will power of the guided agent, where for example a person is created with free will and certain other powers to be in numerous places, those places are also created. And there is the true power to influence something and to transition from being in place a to being in place b, or from being in state a to being in state b as indicated in the following verse:
Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve their allies are the evil ones. They take them out of the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
(Quran: 2/257)
You will surely experience state after state. 
(Quran: 84/19)
So the free will power interacts with fashioning and is not a property reducible and equal to the fashioning of Allah. Fashioning relates more to pattern-like aspects, restrictions. Free will relates to choosing. Guidance relates to the intention and power of making or influencing toward one place or state as opposed to another. Guidance of Allah concerning human beings may also relate to His mercy and grace or the opposite in case of evil human beings. Free will consequences are dynamic as opposed to the restrictions of fashioning.
Regarding the above, the fall of a rock, the orbiting of a planet, the movement of a galaxy and so on, in other words, the movements of all things, the transitions from any states are the examples and implications of the guidance of Allah.
Question 158.  
Is not guidance just a type of all-powerfulness? So why would it be an additional element on top of all-powerfulness and why would it give any additional power to the unitary proof of God? Again why would not the same be true for the power to fashion and to will? 
Answer 158.  
While the pure power is necessary for the guidance by God, the end and with respect to the end the purpose are also necessary for guidance. Likewise, knowledge and fashioning powers are distinct from His guidance: Knowledge is essentially indifferent compared to guidance. His knowledge about �what will result in what� is not in and of itself a guidance. Delivering specific knowledge may be in certain occasions a guidance, but not necessarily. Likewise, by fashioning a being, God may have ascribed to it ends which are good and compliant with the design of that being, and ends which are non-compliant with that design. However, by guidance, God may specifically lead to a certain end; this end may be good or evil for that being. Likewise, the free will power of God is also necessary for guidance. However, it is not sufficient since it does not contain necessarily an end (for a being) in and of itself. God may will a specific end for a being or its opposite; this is entailed by His free will power. But guidance necessitates an end to which the being is directed, but free will power of God does not have necessarily and specifically an end. On the other hand, as the guiding power has above-noted distinctive element on top of pure power, the fashioning power has the elements explained in part 1.4 and free will power has elements explained in part 1.6. additionally to the pure power explained in part 1.9.

And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers."

1.10.1.1.3 The Properties Entailed and Necessitated by Guidance
The properties entailed by the sustaining property �guidance� are as follows:
1.10.1.1.3.1 Unity & Transcendence
The power to guide entails a unitary power to encompass the guided, the end to which he is guided, the initial state or position among other things. As it is related to the power of transcending two or more things, it is also related to the sustaining property �unity�. 
1.10.1.1.3.2 Powerfulness
Although guidance is mostly related to the intention of the guide, it is not only about will but also a power to act. 
Guidance is closely related to power: For example, to guide her kitten, the cat in the earlier example needs to be able to walk along her kitten or be able to make her kitten hear her voice. Likewise, to guide through stars, the God must be able to create a star and make it emit light.
While powerfulness is essentially more about making a change regardless of the direction, guidance is more about the direction of the change. 
1.10.1.1.3.3 Fashioning
The structure of a being may entail a certain preferable direction and guidance. Hence, a guidance toward a good end requires a knowledge about the structure of the guided and its environment. Moreover, guidance entails the existence of the guided, hence, the fashioning of the guided is in this respect an element of ultimate and self-sufficient guidance.
Regarding the position of an agent with respect to a set of relations and relata, a person is an irreducible relatum, he is in one place, and then in another within a fashioned set of relations. The position is not reducible to a smaller or simpler thing or entity within the limited universe. Guidance influences the positions or states of the guided.
On the other hand, fashioning is more related to forming beings, entities, structures, and relations. Fashioning is about a relation, guidance is about alternatives, giving a direction, or alternative and giving the power to choose a good alternative.
1.10.1.1.3.4 Knowledge
When one is guided it is essentially through the acquisition of knowledge. For example, a navigation device gives us knowledge about the state of the road ahead. As explained in part 1.8 knowledge is crucial even with respect to the movements of the physical entities. 
However, knowledge or communicating knowledge does not necessarily equal guidance since a knowledge may be inconsequential regarding an act toward an end. 
1.10.1.1.3.5 Self-Sufficiency
If a thing is not self-sufficient, it cannot be a self-sufficient guide. Therefore, self-sufficiency is important for an ultimate source of guidance.
A self-sufficiently exercised guidance property is necessary, for example, because of the impossibility of infinite regress, regardless of whether that property is within the limited universe or not.
1.10.1.1.3.6 Goodness
While guidance is not necessarily toward a �good� end, we sentient beings essentially expect it to be good; a guidance toward an evil end is not wanted. 
The most important guidance with respect to human beings is the guidance toward the overal truth in all its dimensions relevant for us: It is �true� that producing, eating, exercising, and smoking gives joy to many people. But their degrees of goodness, performance, and implications are also true for each. So, it is also true that smoking is harmful. Hence, the overall truth encompasses the fact that each thing is true together with its implications, harms, benefits, the degrees and priorities of these harms and benefits. Therefore, the truth does not entail running after every peace of truth, but rather targeting and acting through an optimization toward important alternatives in a balanced way. At the end, every person will reach a degree of success in accordance with what he or she targeted and attained as underlined in the following verse:
And for all are degrees from what they have done. And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
(Quran: 6/132)
And the implications of what we do, and their degrees are also true. Therefore the guidance to truth is important in that it may help the guided to reach a good end. However, the guided, as a human being needs to be serious and truthful, comply with the truth. What is done on the part of a Creator and Sustainer, is giving guidance; and this is an important element of His goodness by which He may help a human being have higher degrees:
We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
(Quran: 6/83)
The degrees with respect to goodness are not reducible to things in the limited universe. Our degrees may increase or decrease, and guidance may be very influential in this respect.
Therefore, there is a reason for the guidance of an all-knower, and this guidance is important. In this respect, the guidance property is directly related to goodness. 
The properties related to goodness have been explained in detail in part 1.7. Therefore, they are not explained here in detail with respect to guidance.

1.10.1.2.1 General Guidance we Observe and Introspect is Irreducible to the Things Within the Limited Universe.
The previous part established that sustaining property �guidance� exists. So, does it originate from the limited universe? Is it reducible to or supervenient upon it? 
As explained in part 1.7.2.1.2.2, oughts exist. The previous part established that guidance exists, hence on top of oughts, there is the guide that guides toward the oughts or their opposites. Hence, there is the transcendence that transcends the oughts that are crucial for guidance.
David Hume, in parallel with a physicalist world view claimed that we cannot get �ought� from �is�. If we cannot get it from an �is� and if the physicalist view that reduces all to the behaviors of matter is true, then there cannot be anything or any being that transcends the oughts. Indeed, if all happens because of its immediate physical causes, then directing or influencing toward an end is impossible. Hence, if guidance does not exist, then all our guiding activities like preparing the manuals about how to use a washing machine lose their distinct effectiveness.
However, every human being and even most animals guide and are guided effectively. Even if a physicalist claims that the guiding processes are reducible to the movements of particles, it can be safely said that they are also guided since they follow certain pathways as opposed to many other contingent ones. Parts 1.1, 1.4, and 1.6 explained key issues related to this last point.
In a physicalist world view, we cannot recognize the reality and distinct effectiveness of any guidance: Particles, waves, or fields move in accordance with certain laws of physics but they can neither be guided nor guide. Because to guide, one thing needs to behave self-sufficiently or be guided.
Likewise, if everything is reducible to things in the limited universe, it is impossible that a person is guided from hating his neighbor to loving him. Since there can be no agent who has a distinctly effective perception of these feelings encompassing two or more agents, and the transition from one state to another, and the distinctly effective events or entities that may have an influence in the layer of sentient agents.
Moreover, the irreducibility of the guidance-related properties cited in part 1.10.1.1.3 to the things within the limited universe are explained in the parts related to those properties. The reasons for the irreducibility of those properties are also applicable in many respects to the irreducibility of guidance to the things within the limited universe: For example, the impossibility of infinite regress shows us that tracing back the guidance infinitely backwards will not provide us with a guidance power within the limited universe unless we recognize a self-sufficiently existent guide; likewise, the impossibility of the emergence of consciousness as explained in part 1.5 shows us that we cannot transition one agent from a specific consciousness-related state to another while we have only the limited things within the limited universe.
The irreducibility of awareness, knowledge, free will power, fashioning power, and other properties which are non-separable from a sustaining guidance property were explained in the above parts. The explanations given there demonstrate in their elements and also by analogy that there is a sustaining property �guidance� self-sufficiently exercised by a self-sufficient essence. This property and the essence that self-sufficiently has this property is at the origin of any guidance we observe.

His certain claimed acts and words can be debunked as well if there is evidence against them and if there is no evidence for them. Obviously, the Quran teaches such an attitude for example regarding the false claims based on the false alleged revelations of God brought by some adherents of some religions. But if a specific act relates to not only the contingent things, but also to the nature of Allah, and contradicts it, then we can say that this act or word is not the word of that ultimate cause. For example if someone brings a message that there are two gods, then this message must be rejected. This word does not show that His claimed and proved properties according to a reliable message are false. But if the message is in harmony or there is no contradiction and if there is sufficient evidence for the words as well, then the essence of words will also be accepted, the truthfulness of the messenger as to his duty as a messenger will be accepted based on evidence.

1.11 Other Properties
Syllogisms with respect to the properties of Allah that are not explained in the above parts similar to those explained above may be constructed. Whether it is a property that relates to His person and/or essence, or one that relates to His actions as we perceive them, the same is true. 
A sustaining property mentioned in the Quran, for which a syllogism is not given above, has an aspect that makes it different than the sustaining properties explained above. For instance the (giving) communication(s) power (kalam) may overlap with His guidance. Yet, He may guide just through an event, or He may communicate without an intention to guide. However, those different aspects of the properties are true even though the essence that has those properties is One and non-separable.
The syllogism about a property not mentioned in this book may be similar to the following:
1. Things in the limited universe entail the necessity of the entity/being/essence that has the Property P and the properties entailed by P. 
2. Things in the limited universe do not have P and the properties entailed by P self-sufficiently.
3. There is a Being above the limited universe, who has P and the properties entailed by P.
The explanations in the above and following parts show sufficiently why the limited universe is not self-sufficient and why there is a being above the limited universe with the above explained sustaining properties. They also show how the limited universe can be analyzed in this context with respect to other properties that are necessary for its existence. 
The properties analyzed through the method used in this book do not constitute an exhaustive list of properties of Allah. Obviously, it is possible that we do not know all properties of the ultimate cause, and there may naturally be many properties of the ultimate cause which are irrelevant for human beings. This irrelevance may also be true for a certain time or under specific conditions.  In different contexts we may learn more properties of the ultimate cause. The ultimate cause obviously has the freedom to behave in different ways under different circumstances, as giving life or making to die. These different behaviors may be called by us human beings as different properties. Yet, it is also likely that we see in our study that the ultimate cause has certain intrinsic properties which are most important for us and which are sufficient to identify the ultimate cause as a God defined with such intrinsic properties. 
For example, though part 1.6 mentioned the sub-elements of the proof of Allah related to free will, the book did not mention the sub-elements of the proof of Allah from love even though Allah has the property as the Lover. Yet, it is not necessary to find all properties of Allah directly and precisely related to the evidences of the proof of Allah. The essential properties of Allah such as His transcendence, power, knowledge� are obviously related to the evidences in this universe. The evidences related to the above-mentioned properties of Allah constitute examples that are sufficient to establish the proof of Allah. Further studies may easily expand these evidences to amplify the related understanding.
Hence, the method in this book does not try to achieve an identification of an exhaustive list of all properties of the ultimate cause.
As those explanations are sufficient in this respect, the reader may understand using the above explanations and examples the other sustaining properties that are cited in the Quran. So, the above explanations are also applicable to a large extent to the sustaining properties that are not analyzed in this book and those properties are also elements of the unitary proof of Allah under the light of the Quran. So, since the above explanations are mostly applicable to the latter properties, the book does not take each of them in detail. D. CONCLUSION
Proving something we do not know is useless, knowing something not sufficiently proven is impossible. This book both explains Allah and proves His existence.
Since Allah does not embody any contingencies in His essence like other god claims whose properties cannot be deduced from empirical observations and sound reasoning, this book does not use inference to the best explanation. Rather, it leads through empirical observations and strong logical chains to the properties and hence to the existence of Allah in a deductive way.
So, when I look back, I see that there have been three distinct features of the proof in this book: 
(1) It has been sufficiently complete: While most proof claims for God give a proof only about some very limited aspects of God, the unitary proof of Allah covers all relevant aspects of Allah. The unitary and dynamic structure of the proof will enable thinkers to extend the proof further so as to cover more aspects of Allah. (2) The unitary and systematic structure of the proof provides the audience with many links to the observed facts and to lots of logical premises and conclusions in many layers so as to check any inconsistency within the proof. (3) Thanks to the absence of ad hoc properties of Allah, His purity and simplicity, the proof of Allah will lead the audience directly to the target, instead of working on two stages of a generic god and then a god of a specific religion with some ad hoc properties which cannot be proven through every observation.
The proof is quite comprehensive. However, it has a clear systematic. The syllogisms for each property of Allah have almost the same structure. The tenth property is an exception to this since it relates more to the revelation of Allah than His essence.
As a result we find out that Allah exists as a Being Who is One, Self-Sufficient, All-Encompassing, Aware, Fashioner, Owner of free will power, All-Knower, All-Powerful, Good, and Guide.

5All sustaining properties are related, so when we say related properties we mean directly related properties that are �more apparent from our perspective� regarding some of our experiences. However, when we say God is self-sufficient, what is self-sufficient? The essence that is aware, that is knower, and also that is omnipotent. Again, if the prophesied person is considered to be the Holy Spirit, then it would speak of himself; why a so called part of god would not be able to speak of himself, and would say only what he hears? If the prophesied person is the Holy Spirit, then clearly nobody would be able to say that the three gods are one god in the same time. In this case there would be three gods, because each would have clearly separate abilities. Additionally, if the Holy Spirit leads with its totally different nature when it comes, what would happen before it came?
